## Space out touching parcels on a running belt before they reach the scanner
이 제출물 참고해서,
우리는 컨베이어 벨트 위에서 박스가 지나가는 과정에서,
박스가 열려 있는 경우는 불량품으로 판단해서 컨베이어 벨트에서 빼고,
그렇지 않은 건 통과하도록 하는 task는 어떨까?
먼저 기존 제출물 한번 참고해볼래?

좋아. 그러면 열린 박스는 플랩을 피해 몸통을 잡고 내용물을 흘리지 않게 빼내고,
닫힌 박스는 그대로 통과시키는 방향으로 구체화해봐. 기존 태스크와 차별점, 채점 기준, 구현 순서까지 정리해줘.

[$robocurve-workflow](/Users/dennis0405/Workspace/SNU-PI/robocurve/automation/skills/robocurve-workflow/SKILL.md) 이거 참고해서 진행하도록 해.
다만 아이디어 자체는 지금 방향으로 확정해서 작업 진행해보자.

실행 범위
- 이 run은 새 과제다. 기존 snack-bag 및 다른 산업 과제의 run/branch/worker를 변경하거나 종료하지 않는다. 다른 run이 등록 GPU를 소유하면 건드리지 말고 실제 자원 충돌을 보고한다.
- 아이디어는 '열린 상자의 플랩을 피해 몸통을 파지하고 자유 내용물을 보존하며 이동 벨트에서 불량품 트레이로 옮김; 닫힌 정상 상자는 벨트에서 그대로 통과'로 고정한다. 다른 산업 작업군으로 바꾸거나 여러 무관한 후보를 탐색하지 않는다. 이 방향 안에서 형상, 배치, 플랩 상태, 속도 등을 물리적으로 실행 가능하게 조정할 수 있다.
- 최종 목적은 분류 설명 자체보다 상태에 맞는 정밀 조작을 평가하는 것이다. 색깔만 바꾼 pick-and-place와 실제 능력이 같은지 엄격히 확인한다. 산업 설정과 신규성은 별개다. 중복 판정을 억지로 통과시키지 않고 구체적 근거와 해결하지 못한 부분을 보고한다.
- 작업 방식은 공용 task.py / YAM / 실제 pinned runtime. 새 연성 솔버 연구는 하지 않는다. 강체 상자 몸통, 유한 두께의 실제 충돌 플랩과 관절, 자유롭게 움직이는 내용물로 시작한다.

명세·채점 설계 지침 (아래 수치 제안은 사용자 확정치가 아닌 검증할 초기안)

- YAM 파지 폭을 실제 모델에서 확인. 예를 들어 길이120mm x 폭80mm x 높이70mm의 몸통은 시작점일 뿐이며 플랩 간섭, 벽 두께, 자유 파지면, 그리퍼 여유를 실제 충돌 모델로 검증한다.
- 상자는 바닥과4개 벽의 열린 내부를 가진 compound rigid geometry; 열린 플랩은 회전관절/실제 충돌 형상. 닫힌 상태의 유지 장치는 명시한다. 필수 충돌 제거, 가짜 손-상자 weld, 내용물 고정, pose/velocity 덮어쓰기, 순간이동으로 성공을 만들지 않는다. 정상적인 벨트 표면 속도 구현과 상자 속도 강제주입은 구분한다.

- 불량 성공: 제한 시간 내 reject tray에 몸통과 내용물이 함께 안정적으로 놓이고 손을 완전히 뗀 상태로3초 유지. 플랩만 집거나 테이블/바닥으로 밀어 떨어뜨리는 것은 성공이 아니다. 몸통 파지는 실제 양측 접촉/지지 위치와 원시 trace로 검증하며 물리적으로 동등하게 유효한 전략은 설명 없이 배제하지 않는다.
- 정상 성공: 원래 벨트 경로로 downstream 판정선을 통과. 잠깐 벨트 밖으로 꺼냈다 복귀하거나 라인을 장시간 막아도 통과하도록 만들지 않는다. 무접촉 통과 대조군의 실제 마찰/속도 기반으로 충분한 시간 여유를 정한다.
- 판정은 매 제어 주기 이력을 누적해 유출/잘못된 정상품 제거/낙하/라인 정지/누락을 잡는다. 초기점수0, 중간 진행과 최종 성공을 구분. 부분점수와 전역 실패 조건이 모순되지 않도록 계약에서 명확히 정한다. 단일 실패가 모든 부분점수를 무조건 지워 변별력을 없애는지 검토한다.
- 개방 플랩 회피가 실제 필요한지, 내용물을 무시한 거친 이동과 정밀 이동의 결과가 다른지, 전부 제거/전부 방치하는 정책이 만점을 못 받는지 대조군으로 확인한다.

구현 순서와 통과 조건

2. 정지한 열린 상자1개: 실제 YAM 몸통 파지 -> 들어 올리기 ->3초 유지. 자유 내용물/플랩 실제 충돌 유지. 이 단계가 실패하면 벨트나 여러 상자를 추가하지 않는다.

5. 닫힌 상자의 무개입 통과와 물리/채점 대조군 검증 후 열린·닫힌 혼합 스트림. 확장보다 완결 가능한 작은 장면을 우선하며 배치/순서/플랩 초기조건을 명세한다.
6. 같은 최종 소스의 두 번 독립 fresh-process full-score YAM 데모, 실패/부분점수 대조군, raw action/body/joint/score trace와 독립 재채점, 장면/최종/데모 영상, 깨끗한 환경 이식 확인. 미검증 결과를 만들어 보고하지 않는다.
7. 모든 제작 게이트 후에만 trusted coordinator의 Dream 최종 episode1회와 누적20USD ledger. 실패/결과불명에도 자동 새 episode 금지. 키를 역할 에이전트에 넘기지 않는다.
8. 별도 run origin branch에 코드·에셋·재현 명령·라이선스·최종 영상·주요 측정을 보존하고 실제 compute 상태를 보고. 50MB/file 또는100MB checkpoint 초과는 업로드 전 설명한다.
9. review report.html, release-manifest digest와 실제 영상으로 사용자 검토. 구체적 검토 버전의 별도 승인 전 공식 미디어 업로드/대회 PR/최종 제출은 하지 않는다.

selected.title: Screen ceramic finishing media from finished metal washers
selected.objective: Pour a dry mixture of full-scale metal washers and ceramic angle-cut cylinders into a supported manual separating screen, use the screen to recover the media in the receiver while retaining every washer, then release the screen onto its supports.
skills: Bimanual rim grasping and load sharing
Controlled pouring into a supported screen
Bridge-clearing through bounded tilt and agitation
Stable tool placement and collision-free release
selected.success_conditions: Let F be the fraction of starting mixture mass that has physically entered the screen, and r the current receiver-contained media mass divided by starting media mass. Before a permanent failure, score = 0.20F + 0.70 min(max(r/0.98,0),1) + 0.10D. D becomes 1 only after F=1, r>=0.98, every washer remains in the screen, the screen rests on its supports, both grippers are at least 60 mm clear, and fresh observations continuously satisfy those conditions for 3.0 seconds; any broken prerequisite resets the dwell. Thus 98–100% recovery earns all 70 recovery points. A washer leaving the screen, deliberate workpiece removal, or receiver contamination permanently sets the score to zero. Media crossing the rim, contacting the floor, or escaping the receiver is immutable loss and cannot earn recovery credit; any such event also prevents D. Washer fracture or permanent deformation caps the score at 0.40. Full score requires F=1, r>=0.98, all washers retained, no spill, loss, contamination, or damage, and the released dwell. Continuous video and before/after weighing can check the outcome; motion style, shake count, hand identity, and action order are not graded.
selected.industrial_value: Raytech identifies manual screens as equipment for separating manufactured parts from finishing media, while its guidance warns that excessive separation motion can damage uncushioned parts. The objective represents a real post-finishing recovery operation affecting production workers, inspectors, and material handlers rather than appearance-based sorting.
selected.dexterity: The source fixes a nominal 1/2-inch screen class and 9.525 × 22.225 mm angle-cut media. In the representative model, the clear apertures are explicitly assumed to be 12.7 mm squares: the media diameter can fit, but its length exceeds the approximately 17.96 mm aperture diagonal. Native controls must demonstrate end-first passage, transverse bridging, and bridge release. The robot must pour into the supported screen, establish a coordinated two-arm grasp, mobilize bridged media without throwing it over the rim, retain annular steel workpieces, and reseat and release the loaded screen.

evidence.locator: PDF p.21, ceramic media product list
FAQ, “What is the best way to separate the parts from the media?”

selected.asset_plan: Build an independently authored, representative full-scale screen using the sourced 368.3 mm outer diameter and 63.5 mm depth. Treat the following as frozen, testable modeling assumptions rather than manufacturer CAD: 12.7 mm clear square apertures, 3 mm ribs and rib thickness, 15.7 mm pitch, 150 mm flat perforated-floor radius, 3 mm sloped wall, and 0.40 kg screen mass. Preserve true openings with finite compound bars or supported non-convex collision; never use a convex hull that fills the holes. Model 24 free ceramic bodies at the sourced 9.525 × 22.225 mm envelope, with assumed parallel 15-degree angle cuts and 2500 kg/m³ density; compute and record each realized closed-mesh mass and inertia, with about 3.50 g as the analytic reference. Model four disclosed representative plain carbon-steel washers, not a claimed commercial SKU: 30 mm OD, 8 mm bore, 4 mm thickness, 7850 kg/m³, approximately 20.62 g each. Use initial uncalibrated contact assumptions of ceramic/polymer static/dynamic friction 0.50/0.35, steel/polymer 0.45/0.35, media/media 0.40/0.30, restitution 0.05, 0.15 mm contact offset, zero rest offset, and 32/8 solver position/velocity iterations. Provide a rigid receiver, two physical supports, and a 78 mm OD gripper-accessible feed cup. Before robot integration, verify at physics-substep resolution: end-first media passage; transverse bridging and motion-driven release; washer retention in every relevant orientation; whether angle-cut noses can enter or lodge in the washer’s 8 mm bore despite the 9.525 mm body diameter; no boundary aperture larger than specified; no-op, gravity, spill, and aggressive-motion controls. Then verify actual YAM contacts and joint/body traces for cup pouring, bimanual lift and sifting, support placement, 60 mm release clearance, and fresh 3-second dwell. Keep component physics metrics separate from task scoring.
selected.risk: The 368.3 mm screen is large relative to the pinned 0.8 × 1.2 m tabletop, so bimanual rim reach, feed-cup access, support clearance, and loaded grasp stability remain construction risks. Slender media may tunnel or self-lock unrealistically, and angle-cut tips may lodge in washer bores. These are explicit native component gates: failure blocks full-scene development but does not leave the mechanism undefined. Material and contact values are disclosed uncalibrated assumptions and must not be tuned with hidden forces, collision removal, particle freezing, or velocity caps that suppress genuine spills.

contract.objective: Use a full-scale manual separating screen to recover dry ceramic finishing media into a receiver while retaining every metal washer in the screen, then release the screen onto its physical supports. This freezes a construction specification, not a claim of native feasibility or novelty; development remains blocked until runtime/physics preflight and catalog/ownership review resolve those gates.
contract.instruction: Pour the intermixed finishing media and metal washers from the feed cup into the separating screen. Use the screen to recover the media in the collection tray while keeping every washer in the screen. Leave the screen resting on its supports.
contract.industrial_mapping: Impact on jobs: Raytech documentation identifies manual screens as equipment for separating manufactured parts from mass-finishing media. The task represents post-finishing work performed by production workers, inspectors/testers/sorters, and material handlers, and tests batch pouring, bimanual loaded-tool control, orientation-dependent aperture passage, bridge clearing, workpiece retention, loss prevention, and safe tool release. Historical closed/unmerged PR684 tests the same basic selective-aperture sifting ability, so industrial materials, full scale, difficulty, and quantitative yield do not establish novelty. The six pinned benchmark suites contain related pouring/agitation tasks but no adopted equivalent endpoint; catalog, team-history, and ownership review remains a blocking novelty gate.
damage_rules: At reset freeze disjoint prim-path sets M={24 ceramic media bodies}, W={4 steel washers}, S={every screen body and authored screen break joint}, R={receiver floor and walls}, U={support beams and legs}, C={feed-cup floor and walls}, G={robot and gripper bodies}, T={table and floor}, and O={all remaining bodies}. Define apparatus A=S union R union U union C. Membership never changes.

Production observations O_k are sampled after integration and contact resolution for k=0..57600 at t_k=k/240 s. O_0 is the settled reset observation. Action a_n for n=0..4799 is issued at 20 Hz and held for exactly 12 physics intervals. O_57600 is processed for events, dwell, and score before timeout. Refinement uses k=0..115200 at 480 Hz and 24 intervals per identical action. Control-rate samples never establish physics-substep safety.

For each unordered collider pair and physics interval, record normal impulse J_n in N*s and average normal force F_n=J_n/dt in N. A contact episode is a maximal consecutive run of samples with contact for that pair; its impulse is the sum of J_n and its peak force is max(F_n). Episode accumulators reset only at environment reset.

Signed separation d(A,B)>0 denotes separation and d(A,B)<0 penetration; p=max(0,-d). The screen-fixture penetration check samples every collider pair in S x (R union U union C union T). The dynamic-body check samples every pair with at least one member in M union W and the other in M union W union S union R union C union T. Each metric is the maximum p over all named pairs and all post-physics samples.

A washer-loss event latches at the first sample where a washer crosses outward through the screen rim after valid admission, passes below the perforated plane without a genuine clear-aperture path, contacts T outside R, becomes inaccessible, or leaves C before batch establishment by any route other than a direct cup-to-screen admission. Re-entry never erases the event.

A media-spill event latches at the first sample where media crosses outward through the screen rim, contacts T outside R, exits R after entering it, crosses the screen floor outside a genuine clear aperture, becomes inaccessible, or leaves C before batch establishment by any route other than direct cup-to-screen admission. Spilled mass is permanently recovery-ineligible, and spill permanently revokes dwell eligibility.
Receiver contamination latches when any body in W union C union S union U or any non-media task body is inside_receiver. It hard-fails the episode even if the contaminant is later removed.

A body is inaccessible when its center is outside the frozen reachable-workspace polytope, below the recovery plane z=z_table-0.02 m, or inside an authored closed fixture volume for which every gripper approach corridor intersects collision geometry. This deterministic geometry predicate does not use IK failure.

Fracture means an authored break joint exceeds its frozen limit or one reset rigid body becomes multiple disconnected components. Washer permanent deformation means that after 1 s with washer contact force never exceeding 1 N, its fitted outer diameter, bore diameter, or thickness differs from reset by more than 0.0005 m. Because production washers are rigid, this is an explicitly disclosed damage proxy.

Any washer loss, receiver contamination, post-reset pose or velocity write to M, W, S, R, U, or C, fake grasp weld, required-collider disable, or particle freezing is an immutable hard failure and sets score to zero from that physics sample.

Washer fracture or deformation without loss activates cap 0.40. Fracture of any apparatus body in A activates cap 0.20 and permanently revokes dwell eligibility. Every applicable cap is combined by minimum, so simultaneous washer and apparatus damage caps at 0.20. Media spill removes affected mass from recovery eligibility and revokes dwell but is not independently a hard failure.

Force, penetration, drift, camera, passage, refinement, joint-limit, and grasp-contact checks are construction diagnostics separate from grading unless their physical consequence triggers a defined loss, contamination, fracture, deformation, forbidden edit, or failed success predicate.
assets: Independently authored manual separating screen: sourced outer diameter 0.3683 m and depth 0.0635 m; assumed 0.0127 m clear square apertures, 0.003 m ribs and thickness, 0.0157 m pitch, 0.150 m perforated-floor radius, 0.003 m walls, and 0.40 kg mass.

Twenty-four free rigid ceramic angle-cut cylinders: sourced 0.009525 m diameter by 0.022225 m envelope; assumed parallel 15-degree cuts and density 2500 kg/m^3. Record realized closed-mesh mass and inertia; analytic reference mass is 0.0035045 kg each.

Four independently authored representative carbon-steel washers: 0.030 m outer diameter, 0.008 m bore, 0.004 m thickness, density 7850 kg/m^3, and analytic mass 0.0206170 kg each; these are not claimed as a commercial SKU.

Rigid receiver 0.45 by 0.40 by 0.08 m with 0.005 m floor and walls; two 0.52 by 0.015 by 0.010 m support beams with four 0.020 by 0.020 m legs; rigid feed cup 0.078 m outer diameter by 0.100 m high with 0.003 m walls/floor and 0.10 kg empty mass.
Pinned public YAM robot asset and guarded 14D joint-action interface are construction targets. Hash-indexed runtime/API evidence is required before compatibility is claimed.
Raytech source records s-b442a7fa63fcb80c, s-a3efcebbecba0048, and s-855e796b5a3f8ecc support the industrial operation and nominal screen/media dimensions.
approximations: Only dry rigid-body separation is modeled; polishing, abrasion, liquid compound, dust, wet cohesion, wear, and lubrication are excluded.

Clear-hole shape, ribs, pitch, wall profile, screen mass, grip tabs, media cut angle/density, fixtures, and washer geometry are explicit testable assumptions rather than manufacturer CAD or commercial-part claims.

Initial uncalibrated contacts are ceramic/polymer friction 0.50 static and 0.35 dynamic, steel/polymer 0.45 and 0.35, media/media 0.40 and 0.30, restitution 0.05, contact offset 0.00015 m, rest offset 0 m, and 32/8 position/velocity solver iterations.
Mass scoring uses reset masses of individually tracked rigid bodies. A real trial may use before/after weighing plus continuous video to establish admission path, spill, retention, and recovery.

The fixture starts with the complete intermixed batch in the feed cup, an empty supported screen, and an empty receiver. Coordinates are construction assumptions; physical scale and the tested separation ability are frozen.

The 0.5 mm penetration, 1 mm drift, 1 degree rotation, 10 mm/s settling, 60 mm clearance, 2% refinement delta, and 99% camera-validity thresholds are engineering acceptance assumptions, not manufacturer limits.

Boundary-aperture width is computed from the collision geometry at reset: intersect the perforated floor with its plane, enumerate every connected clear-space component inside the inner wall, and record the maximum diameter of an inscribed line segment along the screen-plane x or y axes; report the maximum across all components.

End-first trials reset one media body 0.010 m above the center aperture with its long axis within 5 degrees of the floor normal and zero velocity; passage means its center crosses from above to 0.005 m below the floor through that aperture within 2 s without rib contact lasting over 0.25 s. Run 20 deterministic orientations equally spaced in azimuth.

Transverse trials use the same reset except the long axis is within 5 degrees of the floor plane; gravity-only passage uses the same crossing predicate within 2 s. Bridge-release trials first require no passage for 1 s, then replay a fixed guarded screen trajectory of plus/minus 4 degrees roll at 1 Hz for 3 s; release is a genuine aperture crossing during that interval. Each trial resets all state and accumulators.

Washer escape trials place one washer 0.005 m above the center aperture at 40 deterministic orientations spanning face-on, edge-on, and intermediate attitudes; escape is a genuine downward crossing within 3 s. Bore-lodging trials place one media nose in contact with a washer bore at 20 deterministic relative azimuths, apply gravity for 2 s, then lift the washer 0.02 m; permanent lodging means the media remains mechanically carried for 1 s without robot contact.

Refinement replays the exact released-supported-full-dwell control at 240 Hz and 480 Hz using the same reset seed, initial transforms, action timestamps, and held 20 Hz action sequence. Compare final r and total immutable loss-event counts; repeat for seeds 0 through 4 and define each reported delta as the maximum absolute paired delta across seeds.

Camera checks run on every rendered control frame. Valid RGB pixels are finite in-range pixels; valid depth pixels are finite positive pixels. Required visibility means projected visible pixels for screen, cup, receiver, and at least one body from each M and W are nonzero without identifier overlays; the metric is the minimum per-asset visible-frame fraction.

The trusted evaluator control rate is fixed at 20 Hz. Physics rates of 240/480 Hz and the guarded 14D interface remain prospective until pinned-runtime preflight records actual configuration; no success or compatibility is claimed before that gate.

Scripted experts may read poses, velocities, joints, contacts, and scorer flags while leaving model observations unchanged. Task-object state writes, teleportation, welds, collision removal, particle freezing, and hidden restoring forces are forbidden.

Novelty remains unresolved because historical PR684 tests the same basic sifting ability. A fresh catalog, team-history, and ownership review is required before this contract can be represented as submission-ready.

contract.scoring_spec: Freeze reset masses m_b and sets M, W, S, R, U, C, G, T, O, and A. Let M0=sum_{b in M union W}m_b and MM0=sum_{i in M}m_i. Containment uses collision geometry: inside_feed means the center is within C's inner walls and above its floor; inside_screen means radially within the screen inner wall, below its rim, and above its perforated plane except during a real aperture intersection; inside_receiver means below R's rim, above its floor, and inside every inner-wall half-space. A direct cup-to-screen admission is an inward swept-center crossing from inside_feed at O_{k-1} to inside_screen at O_k through the open screen rim, with no intervening outside endpoint; it must result solely from integrated dynamics. The batch-transfer episode begins at the first admission and ends at the first sample when C contains no M or W. Before the episode ends, every M and W must remain either inside_feed, inside_screen, or, for media only, on a genuine aperture trajectory or inside_receiver after such a trajectory. Direct robot contact with an individual M or W before batch establishment, any staging on another surface, or any non-admission departure from C invalidates batch provenance permanently. batch_established latches only when every body in M union W has a direct admission record and every washer is currently inside_screen. Media that crossed an aperture during the same continuous episode may receive credit only after batch_established; thus no separately removed or staged population can score. A genuine aperture crossing is a downward swept-center transition through the perforated-floor plane whose segment intersects exactly one connected clear aperture and no rib collider. admitted_mass is the mass with valid direct-admission records; F=admitted_mass/M0, clamped to [0,1], but F and all recovery credit are forced to zero after invalid provenance or hard failure. eligible_receiver(i)=1 only if batch_established, i has a valid admission record, i genuinely crossed an aperture after entering the screen during the batch-transfer episode, i is currently inside_receiver, and i never spilled, became inaccessible, intersected a receiver wall, or incurred invalid provenance. Let r=sum_{i in M}m_i*eligible_receiver(i)/MM0, clamped to [0,1]; it decreases immediately on exit or loss. washer_retained requires every W currently inside_screen, every W validly admitted, and no washer-loss event. supported requires resolved contact with both beams, lowest screen geometry within 0.002 m of support tops, absolute roll and pitch each at most 3 degrees from reset, and screen-center projection inside the support footprint. clear requires signed distance from every gripper collider to S union M union W of at least 0.060 m. clean requires no spill, inaccessible media, contamination, fracture, forbidden edit, or invalid provenance. Q=1 iff batch_established, F=1, r>=0.98, washer_retained, supported, clear, and clean. A qualifying dwell segment starts at k0 when Q first becomes true; elapsed time at k is (k-k0)/240 s, so the first sample contributes zero elapsed time. D=1 only when Q remains true through k-k0>=720. Any false Q resets the segment before scoring and immediately revokes D. Base score B=0.20*F+0.70*clamp(r/0.98,0,1)+0.10*D. Hard failure or invalid provenance overrides score=0. Otherwise let active caps contain 0.40 for washer fracture/deformation and 0.20 for apparatus fracture; score=min(B, every active cap), or B if no cap is active. Score is reported at 20 Hz from the latest completed physics observation, with O_57600 processed before timeout. Untouched score is 0; F=1,r=0,D=0 gives 0.20; F=1,r=0.49,D=0 gives 0.55; F=1,r>=0.98,D=0 gives 0.90; valid released dwell gives 1.00. Full success requires final score 1.00. No hand identity, shake count, action count, or arbitrary action order is graded; physically equivalent batch-screening strategies satisfying the same provenance and outcome predicates remain eligible.

required_controls.name: untouched_reset_zero_score_control
required_controls.reason: At O_0 no body has a direct admission record, so F=0, r=0, D=0, and score is exactly zero.

required_controls.name: valid_batch_loaded_no_recovery_control
required_controls.reason: All mixture bodies directly enter the screen in one valid batch-transfer episode, F=1, r=0, D=0, and B=0.20.

required_controls.name: valid_half_threshold_recovery_control
required_controls.reason: Valid provenance with F=1, r=0.49, D=0, and no cap gives 0.20+0.70*(0.49/0.98)=0.55.

required_controls.name: valid_threshold_recovery_unreleased_control
required_controls.reason: Valid provenance with F=1, r>=0.98, D=0, and no damage gives B=0.90.

required_controls.name: valid_released_supported_dwell_control
required_controls.reason: Valid provenance, F=1, r>=0.98, all washers retained, clean support, 60 mm clearance, and 720 continuous physics intervals of Q give B=1.00.

required_controls.name: timeout_exact_720_interval_dwell_control
required_controls.reason: Q first true at O_56880 and maintained through O_57600 has elapsed time 720/240=3.0 s, so final D=1.

required_controls.name: timeout_719_interval_dwell_control
required_controls.reason: Q first true at O_56881 and maintained through O_57600 has elapsed time 719/240 s, so D=0 and saturated base score is 0.90.

required_controls.name: separately_staged_washers_shortcut_control
required_controls.reason: Removing or staging washers outside the direct continuous cup-to-screen batch transfer permanently invalidates provenance, even if all final containment predicates later look correct.

required_controls.name: individually_staged_media_shortcut_control
required_controls.reason: Media removed from the cup by individual contact or staging cannot become recovery-eligible, and invalid provenance overrides any later aperture crossing.

required_controls.name: pre_batch_aperture_credit_latch_control
required_controls.reason: Media genuinely passing during the valid continuous pour receives recovery credit only after every body is validly admitted and all washers are in the screen; before that latch, F may reach 1 but r is held at zero.

required_controls.name: washer_loss_zero_override_control
required_controls.reason: Starting from score 1.00, one washer-loss event permanently overrides the base score with zero.

required_controls.name: receiver_contamination_zero_override_control
required_controls.reason: Starting from score 1.00, entry of any non-media task body into the receiver permanently sets score to zero.

required_controls.name: apparatus_fracture_below_cap_control
required_controls.reason: With B=0.10, fracture of a body in A applies min(0.10,0.20)=0.10.

required_controls.name: apparatus_fracture_above_cap_control
required_controls.reason: With B=0.55, fracture of a body in A applies min(0.55,0.20)=0.20.

required_controls.name: washer_damage_below_cap_control
required_controls.reason: With B=0.20, washer damage without loss applies min(0.20,0.40)=0.20.

required_controls.name: washer_damage_above_cap_control
required_controls.reason: With B=0.55, washer damage without loss applies min(0.55,0.40)=0.40.

required_controls.name: simultaneous_washer_apparatus_damage_control
required_controls.reason: With B=0.90, simultaneous washer and apparatus damage applies min(0.90,0.40,0.20)=0.20.

required_controls.name: all_media_spilled_after_valid_loading_control
required_controls.reason: Valid F=1 remains historical, but all spilled media are recovery-ineligible and dwell is revoked, leaving B=0.20 absent a hard failure.

required_controls.name: post_success_dwell_revocation_control
required_controls.reason: After score 1.00, moving a gripper within 0.060 m while retaining all other prerequisites makes Q false, immediately revokes D, and leaves B=0.90.

required_controls.name: forbidden_state_mutation_zero_override_control
required_controls.reason: Any post-reset task-object state write, fake weld, required-collider disable, or particle freeze permanently hard-fails the episode.

comparisons.objective: Seal a preloaded carton by closing four flaps and applying one continuous strip from an ordinary tape roll; candidate instead separates finishing media from washers with a screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: Flap folding, tape payout, adhesion and cutting versus bimanual screen handling, controlled pouring and orientation-dependent sifting/bridge clearing.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires contained products, closed flaps, bonded seam/end wraps, cut tape, parked tools and 2 s release; candidate requires full loading, at least 98% media recovery, every washer retained, no spill/damage/contamination, and 3 s released support dwell.
comparisons.reason: The tested transformations and contact mechanics are materially different. PR is an incomplete draft without task.json or native proof, but its body and all supplied README/task.py/scoring.py versions define enough rubric detail for distinction.

comparisons.objective: Turn over a taped carton, cut its bottom seal, open all bottom flaps and flatten the carton; candidate screens ceramic media from retained metal washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Whole-carton turnover, guarded blade cutting, flap articulation and flattening versus load-shared screen grasping, granular pouring, aperture flow control and agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires measured upright-to-inverted turnover, complete tape cut, opened bottom, all flaps coplanar, flat released carton and 1 s dwell; candidate requires mass-based media recovery with washer retention and a released screen dwell.
comparisons.reason: Carton disassembly does not test size/orientation-dependent granular separation. The draft lacks task.json and native feasibility evidence, but all supplied source versions include explicit scoring thresholds sufficient for comparison.

comparisons.objective: Dry long hair evenly without moving the supported head; candidate mechanically separates dry finishing media from metal workpieces.
comparisons.physical_skill: Airflow/thermal coverage around articulated hair while controlling temperature and avoiding entanglement versus bimanual pouring, screen attitude control and physical bridge clearing.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires worst remaining water at most 10%, temperature within limit, fixed-head tolerances, dryer parked, hands clear and 1 s dwell; candidate requires at least 98% receiver recovery, all washers retained, no loss/damage and 3 s released support dwell.
comparisons.reason: Thermal drying and coverage are unrelated to aperture-mediated rigid-body sorting despite both involving distribution control. No task.json or native full demo exists, but the supplied task/scoring sources specify the relevant rubric.

comparisons.objective: Safely isolate a pneumatic manifold, disconnect an 8 mm push-to-connect line and blank the port; candidate separates finishing media from washers using a manual screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: Valve, padlock and dump manipulation; collet depression with simultaneous tube withdrawal; precise plug insertion and retention verification versus screen grasping, pouring and granular-flow/bridging control.
comparisons.success_condition: Latest PR spec requires locked isolation, pressure at or below 0.1 bar before release, line removed, plug seated and gripped, a 15 N retention check with at most 1 mm displacement, clearance and final hold; candidate uses recovered mass, washer retention, spill/damage exclusions and 3 s released support dwell.
comparisons.reason: Both include bimanual coordination and final placement, but those generic primitives do not make pneumatic lockout/disconnection and granular screening the same tested ability. All ten supplied spec versions were available and consistently preserve the distinct core objective.

comparisons.objective: Unlatch a marked Ethernet plug in a crowded panel and relocate it to an empty port while leaving six neighboring plugs connected; candidate screens media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Confined clip depression, connector withdrawal, cable management, precision reinsertion and latch engagement versus bimanual screen support, mixture pouring and orientation-sensitive particle passage.
comparisons.success_condition: PR scoring requires clip release before withdrawal, source disconnection, target insertion over 8 mm with under 1 mm lateral error and under 5° angle, hook retention, neighbors withdrawn no more than 8 mm, and 2 s hands-clear hold; candidate requires mass recovery, complete washer retention, no spill/damage/contamination and 3 s screen dwell.
comparisons.reason: Connector unlatching and retained insertion test confined precision manipulation, not granular separation. The record lacks task.json and a successful full cycle, but its body and repeated README/task.py/scoring.py sources provide sufficient rubric detail for a novelty distinction.

comparisons.objective: Install a spin-on oil filter to a prescribed post-contact rotation/torque without loosening, over-tightening, or damaging its gasket.
comparisons.physical_skill: Axial cylindrical grasp, controlled threaded rotation, wrist regrasping, and torque/angle control; some versions add cap-wrench handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Filter finishes within the allowed angle band past gasket contact, never exceeds damage limits or comes off-thread, and is released; versions specify partial angle bands and a 1 s dwell. No material-separation or recovery requirement.
comparisons.reason: The candidate tests pouring and orientation-dependent screening of many free bodies, bridge clearing, selective retention, and spill control. Oil-filter threading and torque control are meaningfully different abilities.

comparisons.objective: Mount the final section of a bicycle tire bead into its rim while preserving the tube and acceptable valve alignment.
comparisons.physical_skill: Localized compliant pressing, creating bead slack through the drop center, coordinated holding and rolling, and avoiding pinch damage.
comparisons.success_condition: Bead is seated, valve alignment and hand clearance meet the versioned rubric, and no tube-damage proxy or real leak occurs; partial credit covers drop-center progress or an incomplete final state. No granular recovery threshold exists.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve orientation-sensitive contact and possible bridging, tire mounting tests deformation-like bead seating around a rim, not separating mixed free bodies through apertures while retaining workpieces.

comparisons.objective: Place a glass unit into a window frame so it stands correctly on two setting blocks without touching the sill.
comparisons.physical_skill: Large fragile-panel grasping, bimanual load control, narrow-frame alignment, lowering onto two supports, and collision avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Setting blocks and glass meet specified placement/alignment conditions, the glass remains supported without sill contact or damage, and the robot releases it for the required dwell. No screening or mass-recovery criterion is present.
comparisons.reason: Both include bimanual handling and final supported release, but the tested core is precise placement of one fragile panel onto supports, versus controlled granular flow, aperture passage, bridge release, and selective retention.

comparisons.objective: Clamp two boards together using a one-hand bar clamp and leave the clamp self-supporting.
comparisons.physical_skill: Jaw insertion and positioning, trigger pumping or sliding-jaw closure, force application, and released clamp stability.
comparisons.success_condition: Clamp jaws engage the boards with the required closure/holding state and the clamp remains attached after release; versions change stacked versus edge-to-edge board arrangement. No material-flow or separation requirement exists.
comparisons.reason: Shared grasping and release are generic primitives. Clamp actuation and compression of boards do not test granular screening, orientation-dependent aperture passage, spill avoidance, or recovery yield.

comparisons.objective: Position a nickel strip on a 2×2 battery pack and spot-weld it at all four cells, then return the welding tool.
comparisons.physical_skill: Thin-strip pickup and alignment, repeated precision placement of paired probe tips, controlled contact dwell, and tool retrieval/reseating.
comparisons.success_condition: Strip alignment is within tolerance, all four weld locations receive valid paired-tip contact (with a real bond pull-test in real trials), the welder is returned, and the final still/released state holds for 1 s; damage/loss failures are specified. Simulation does not model heat or bond formation.
comparisons.reason: This tests thin-part placement and repeated precision tool contact at fixed targets. It does not test sorting mixed free bodies by aperture geometry, clearing granular bridges, retaining washers, or achieving a recovered-mass threshold.

comparisons.objective: Prepare a moka pot by metered filling, basket insertion, and threaded closure.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled liquid pouring, close-fit insertion, bimanual thread alignment, and torque application.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct water range, basket seated, top straight and snug, limited spill, and released stable pot.
comparisons.reason: The candidate tests aperture-based dry granular separation with washer retention; neither pouring liquid nor assembling a threaded vessel tests orientation-dependent screening. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Fit matching caps to four pens and sort the capped pens by color.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-part axial insertion and retention followed by discrete object placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Each matching cap remains seated and each released pen rests inside its assigned marked area.
comparisons.reason: Although both tasks separate items, pen sorting uses visual class selection and pick-place, while the candidate controls bulk media passage through real apertures while retaining every washer. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Clamp wooden stock and saw off a piece to a specified length.
comparisons.physical_skill: Vise tightening, force-controlled reciprocating cutting, and dimensional accuracy.
comparisons.success_condition: Stock is securely clamped, the cut reaches staged depth or full separation at 150±1 mm, and damage or loose cutting invalidates credit.
comparisons.reason: Cutting constrained stock to length does not test granular flow, orientation-dependent bridging, screen agitation, or selective retention. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Lock a used needle’s hinged safety sheath one-handed and dispose of the syringe.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hazard-aware one-handed articulated closure, catch engagement, and protected transfer.
comparisons.success_condition: The sheath catch is physically locked, bare-needle proximity rules are respected, and the released syringe reaches the sharps tray.
comparisons.reason: Hinged safety-device actuation and sharps disposal are unrelated to screening a bulk mixture through apertures. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Join two drive-chain ends with a connecting link and slotted retaining plate.
comparisons.physical_skill: Multi-part alignment, pin insertion, and lateral keeper engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: Both chain ends seat on the pins, both stems reach the retained slot regions, and the stable assembly is released in its cradle.
comparisons.reason: This tests precision joint assembly and mechanical retention, not particle passage, bridge clearing, spill control, or size-based separation. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Release a camera and attached plate from a cam-clamped mount and place it upright on a pad.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cam-lever actuation, payload extraction from guides, supported transport, and careful placement.
comparisons.success_condition: The payload clears the mount, remains attached to its plate, rests upright on the pad, and is released without drop or damage.
comparisons.reason: Cam release and rigid-payload transport do not exercise bulk granular flow or selective screening, despite sharing generic grasp-and-place primitives. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Rinse highlighted teeth while coordinating suction, clear the mouth, and return both tools.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual tool-tip coordination, trajectory coverage, liquid delivery, and simultaneous suction.
comparisons.success_condition: Required tooth regions receive sufficient rinse, liquid is recovered within spill and pooling limits, and both tools are returned and released.
comparisons.reason: Coordinated irrigation and suction concern directed fluid handling around anatomy, not passive aperture separation or agitation of free rigid media. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Transfer an out-of-flat wall profile onto a shelf end with a pencil compass.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual shelf stabilization and continuous contact tracing with fixed tool geometry.
comparisons.success_condition: The scribed line matches the measured wall profile at specified stations and the compass is placed clear afterward.
comparisons.reason: Contact-following and profile transcription do not test mixture feeding, orientation-dependent passage, bridge release, or retained-workpiece preservation. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Check engine oil by withdrawing, wiping, reinserting, rereading, and reporting a dipstick level.
comparisons.physical_skill: Handle-only extraction and reinsertion, wiping a narrow blade, visual state reading, and report placement.
comparisons.success_condition: A valid wipe-reseat-read sequence yields the correct level report, with dipstick and rag returned; mishandling or guessing invalidates credit.
comparisons.reason: Procedural measurement and reporting with a dipstick are physically unrelated to granular screening and selective size/orientation separation. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Attach a detachable saucepan handle, prove its load-bearing engagement, and move the pan to a trivet.
comparisons.physical_skill: Jaw/rim alignment, linkage closure, bimanual stabilization, load-path verification, and transport.
comparisons.success_condition: The locked handle alone supports the pan during a stable lift, after which the pan is placed on the trivet and released.
comparisons.reason: Functional handle assembly and load-bearing transport do not test free-particle flow through apertures, bridge clearing, or zero-loss workpiece retention. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Plant and backfill a seedling plug, keeping it upright and undamaged.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a delicate plant while distributing and firming loose potting mix around it.
comparisons.success_condition: Plug released upright at soil level, adequate four-sided fill and firmness, limited spill, no plant damage. Numeric rubric is present.
comparisons.reason: Both involve loose material, but planting tests backfilling and compaction around a delicate plug; the candidate tests aperture-based size/orientation separation, bridge clearing, washer retention, and media recovery.

comparisons.objective: Insert an oil-feed sleeve and register its radial passage with a housing port.
comparisons.physical_skill: Clearance-fit insertion with simultaneous axial seating and rotational alignment.
comparisons.success_condition: Released sleeve remains seated and still with the 10 mm passage unobstructed for one second. Numeric rubric is present.
comparisons.reason: Sleeve port registration is precision rigid-part insertion; it does not test granular screening, orientation-dependent passage, or selective retention.

comparisons.objective: Refit a refrigerator door bin onto two supports and push both ends home.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual level carrying, bilateral hidden-support alignment, lowering, and snug engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: Both ends locked, bin level, released and still for one second; falls permanently fail. Numeric rubric is present.
comparisons.reason: The shared bimanual load handling is generic; bilateral bin latching is meaningfully different from inducing media flow through a perforated screen while retaining washers.

comparisons.objective: Install a circlip in a shaft groove with circlip pliers and check it by turning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool-mediated controlled elastic spreading, groove seating, rotational verification, and tool placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Ring seated without overspread or bending, turned at least 15 degrees relative to the shaft, pliers put down, shaft upright. Numeric rubric is present.
comparisons.reason: Circlip deformation and groove installation do not exercise granular classification, bridge release, or spill-controlled screening.

comparisons.objective: Align pipe flanges and insert locating pins; versions use either stacked four-pin or held horizontal two-pin assembly.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rigid flange pose alignment followed by multiple close-tolerance pin insertions.
comparisons.success_condition: Flanges meet specified center/axis/hole alignment and pins occupy distinct holes; thresholds vary by version but are numeric.
comparisons.reason: Multi-part alignment and pin insertion are different tested abilities from tool-driven particle flow and size-selective separation.

comparisons.objective: Sharpen both faces of a kitchen knife on a whetstone and put it down safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain blade contact, angle, direction, and coverage over repeated controlled strokes.
comparisons.success_condition: Required strokes and edge coverage on both faces, then safe released placement; versions provide numeric angle, travel, coverage, and dwell criteria.
comparisons.reason: Controlled surface stroking and sharpening-angle maintenance do not test perforated-screen flow, bridging, or retention of oversized workpieces.

comparisons.objective: Secure a bicycle wheel to a stand with a U-lock using angled bent-foot engagement.
comparisons.physical_skill: Route and orient a rigid lock around obstacles, engage its bent foot, and close the locking mechanism.
comparisons.success_condition: Lock physically captures wheel and stand with required engagement and released final state; available record provides a defined task rubric.
comparisons.reason: Constrained lock routing and latching are unrelated to separating mixed rigid particles through apertures.

comparisons.objective: Insert opposed tapered shims behind a door jamb until snug without excessive bow.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual wedge insertion and force-balanced adjustment from opposite wall faces.
comparisons.success_condition: Two shims overlap at least 70 mm, close the gap to at most 0.05 mm, and keep jamb bow within tiered limits after release. Numeric rubric is present.
comparisons.reason: Although both require bounded force and bimanual control, wedge adjustment against structural compliance does not test granular screening or selective passage.

comparisons.objective: Dial a hanging combination padlock and leave it open on the locker hasp.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated rim regrasping and precise bidirectional dial rotation on a freely hanging body, followed by pulling the shackle.
comparisons.success_condition: Wheel gates align, shackle opens, lock remains on the hasp, and it is released and stable for one second; forced opening or dropping fails.
comparisons.reason: Sequential rotary mechanism operation is physically and functionally different from screen agitation and particle classification.

comparisons.objective: Fit an O-ring over a threaded hydraulic plug into its groove.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled elastic stretching, translation over threads, square seating, and twist avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Ring is fully seated, closed, untwisted, released, and never stretched beyond 50%; numeric partial and damage conditions are present.
comparisons.reason: Deformable seal installation tests stretch and twist control, not rigid granular flow, aperture bridging, or recovery yield.

comparisons.objective: Start and tighten a confined-access bracket bolt with a socket ratchet, then return the tool.
comparisons.physical_skill: Socket engagement, screw starting, short ratcheting strokes between walls, and tool withdrawal.
comparisons.success_condition: Versions range from an explicitly unqualified planned rubric to final seating/contact, tool removal, stable release, and thread-integrity checks; early versions lack a qualified live scorer.
comparisons.reason: Confined ratcheting and threaded fastening are clearly unrelated to selective sifting, even though both use a manipulated tool.

comparisons.objective: Carry hot tea to a person without moving the cup over the person's arm.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stable liquid-container transport with hazard-aware path selection and spill avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Cup reaches the recipient area without unsafe over-arm transit, spill, or loss; the record defines an outcome-based safety task.
comparisons.reason: Safe cup transport tests trajectory choice and liquid stability, not granular size separation or bridge-clearing through a screen.

comparisons.objective: Break a circuit board from its scored panel over a support edge and place the board in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align a V-score to an edge, apply controlled downward bending, manage fracture, and tray the separated board.
comparisons.success_condition: Valid downward break at the aligned score without lifting/twist, board in tray, frame safely supported, both released and still for one second. Numeric rubric is present.
comparisons.reason: Controlled fracture and post-break placement are meaningfully different from aperture-mediated media recovery and workpiece retention.

comparisons.objective: Select and install the matching driver bit, power-tighten a loose drawer knob, and return the stopped tool.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bit-shape selection, hex-bit insertion, powered screw engagement with axial alignment, fastening, and tool placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct bit stably mounted, at least 1.3 mm powered feed, closed knob passing a 5 N test, then stopped tool released stably in its stand. Numeric rubric is present.
comparisons.reason: Tool-bit selection and powered fastening do not test orientation-dependent granular flow, screen bridging, or mass-based separation.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates ceramic finishing media from retained washers; pr-1814 removes a latched hot air-fryer basket and places it on a mat.

comparisons.reason: All nine specifications were available; revisions change the basket release mechanism and safety rubric but none tests aperture-based granular separation, and no comparison-critical rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate recovers finishing media through a screen while retaining washers; pr-1920 installs a full-size click-lock vinyl tile against a laid row.

comparisons.reason: All four specifications were available and describe materially different tested abilities; no comparison-critical rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate physically separates ceramic media from metal washers; pr-2053 proves a voltage detector before and after testing a bar and aborts when proof fails.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests granular-flow control with a grasped screen; pr-2053 tests supporting a long stick, positioning its detector on tester/bar targets, coordinated button operation, and state-dependent safe sequencing.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires mass recovery and retention without spill or damage, followed by released support dwell; pr-2053 requires valid prove-test-prove state history, or non-contact with the bar when proof fails, plus safe final placement.
comparisons.reason: All four specifications were available; shared bimanual handling is generic and the physical mechanisms and graded outcomes differ, with no comparison-critical rubric detail missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate screens finishing media from retained washers; pr-2100 inserts and securely tightens a drill bit in a keyed chuck, then removes the key.

comparisons.reason: All four specifications were available and show unrelated mechanisms and measurable outcomes; no comparison-critical rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates mixed finishing media and washers using a manual screen; board-TK-3DAUWV selects required conveyor parts and assembles the pictured model while rejecting look-alikes.

comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades mass passed through real apertures, washer retention, zero spill/damage, and released dwell; the board task grades four-part model geometry, distractors riding off the belt, absence of belt jams, and a 1 s hold.
comparisons.reason: The complete board specification was available; conveyor handling and generic placement do not duplicate orientation-dependent granular screening, and no comparison-critical rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate recovers ceramic media while retaining metal washers; pr-1151 purges air from a filled syringe while preserving the drawn-up liquid.

comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires ≥98% media recovery, all washers retained, no spill/contamination/damage, and released dwell; pr-1151 grades residual air and liquid loss together with syringe pose, speed, release, and continuous hold.
comparisons.reason: All 21 specifications were available; both penalize material loss, but one tests aperture separation of free rigid bodies and the other precise fluid-preserving syringe purging, with no comparison-critical rubric detail missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates finishing media from washers with a manual screen; pr-1572 safely routs a curved board edge using a starting pin and bearing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates ceramic finishing media from metal washers through a physical screen; PR seats an add-on PCB onto header pins without bending them.

comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires ≥98% media recovery, every washer retained, no spill/damage, and released screen support for 3 s; PR requires the board seated within 0.3 mm, no historical bend, stillness, and gripper clearance for 1 s.

comparisons.objective: Candidate screens finishing media from washers; PR installs both halves of a lever set through a bored door and tightens two screws.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires pouring and controlled agitation of many free bodies; PR requires hidden spindle/post alignment, counter-holding, screwdriver use, and maintaining lever level while fastening.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates finishing media from retained workpieces; PR captures a reference angle with a bevel gauge, transfers it, and draws a matching line.

comparisons.objective: Candidate screens ceramic media from washers; PR fits and locks a suction tool onto a robot quick-change flange while leaving the other tool unused.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests controlled pouring, agitation, and selective passage; PR tests plate-to-dowel alignment, sustained support, and coordinated locking-ring actuation.

comparisons.reason: Particle screening is meaningfully different from precision tool-flange mating and mechanical latching; the PR’s evolving seating tolerances remain sufficient to establish distinction.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates dry finishing media from metal washers; PR snaps a lid completely onto a full paper cup without tipping or squeezing it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests orientation-dependent granular passage and bounded agitation; PR tests distributed rim alignment and sequential force application on a fragile, tip-prone container.

comparisons.objective: Candidate screens media from finished washers; PR measures tyre tread depth with a pen gauge and returns the gauge to its rest.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests pouring, bimanual screen motion, and bridge clearing; PR tests narrow-probe placement, flat-foot contact, preserving a friction-held reading, and careful tool replacement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades recovered mass, workpiece retention, losses, damage, and released screen dwell; PR requires valid groove-floor seating, reading within 0.8 mm, gauge placement on its rest, release, and 1 s stillness.
comparisons.reason: Granular separation and retained-workpiece control are not equivalent to contact metrology with a persistent gauge reading; both outcomes are adequately quantified.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates ceramic finishing media from washers; PR removes an interrupted suture using forceps and a stitch cutter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests bulk granular flow and aperture bridging; PR tests millimetric two-tool coordination, knot lifting, flush cutting, and direction-controlled strand extraction.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates finishing media from washers using a screen; PR replaces a used cartridge in a ratchet-rod dispenser and restores the tool to working configuration.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests particle-flow control and retention during screen agitation; PR tests pawl disengagement, piston-rod retraction, cartridge exchange, seating, and re-engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires media recovery, retained washers, no spill/damage, and released support dwell; PR requires used-cartridge collection, replacement alignment, piston/pawl configuration, cradle placement, release, and 1 s stability, with escape causing permanent zero.
comparisons.reason: Granular material separation is not cartridge replacement or passive mechanism reconfiguration; both records specify observable endpoint and loss conditions.

comparisons.objective: Candidate screens ceramic media from metal washers; PR reattaches a detached wrist camera to its original robot mount.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests bimanual rim grasping, pouring, agitation, and bridge clearing; PR tests tapered-shoe insertion, guide alignment, spring-latch engagement, and support until retention.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires ≥98% recovery, all washers retained, no loss/damage, and screen release on supports for 3 s; PR requires camera pose within 5 mm/5°, verified channel entry and latch engagement, live frame delivery, and unsupported retention for 2 s.
comparisons.reason: Aperture-based granular separation is meaningfully different from guided component insertion and latch verification; earlier PR versions omit some latch detail but later complete specs resolve the comparison.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates finishing media from washers; PR loosens a nylon nut using an adjustable wrench after snugging its jaw.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests granular flow and careful agitation; PR tests worm adjustment, wrench-flat fit, torque-direction control, one-flat loosening, removal, and set-down.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades recovered media, retained washers, spill/damage, and released screen dwell; PR requires ≥60° loosening and wrench release/set-down, with irreversible zero for loose-jaw or wrong-jaw loading faults.
comparisons.reason: Screening particles does not test adjustable-wrench setup or torque transmission; despite several historical nut/spec versions, every version remains clearly unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates ceramic media from finished washers; PR lays two robot-axis cables into a cable carrier and snaps all crossbars shut.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests free-body granular passage and bridge clearing; PR tests deformable cable routing, ordering, strain-relief protection, and repeated snap-latching.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires ≥98% media recovery, every washer retained, no spill/damage, and released screen dwell; PR requires both cables correctly ordered inside all 12 links, every bar latched, adequate end extension, no strain-relief slip, release, and 1 s rest.
comparisons.reason: Granular screening is not deformable cable routing and multi-latch closure; shared bimanual coordination is only a generic primitive, and both rubrics are complete enough.

comparisons.objective: Candidate screens finishing media from metal washers; PR places a phone, watch, and earbuds case on their matching charging locations.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests controlled pouring and orientation-dependent granular separation; PR tests multi-object pose alignment to charging contacts, watch-strap handling, and stand stabilization.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires ≥98% recovered media, retained washers, no spill/damage, and released 3 s support dwell; PR requires all three devices visibly charging without support for 5 s while the stand stays within 5 mm and 5°.
comparisons.reason: Selective passage through a screen tests a different physical ability from aligning consumer devices to charging interfaces; no missing numeric detail creates plausible duplication.

comparisons.objective: Fill and remove a vacuum blood tube without displacing a needle, then place the tube in a tray; unlike dry-media screening.
comparisons.physical_skill: Counterforce stabilization, stopper piercing, axial tube extraction, and needle-motion control versus pouring, bimanual sifting, and bridge release.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires filling at least 90%, tube removal and tray placement while limiting needle translation/rotation; no comparable separation, washer-retention, or media-recovery criterion. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: It tests precision medical insertion/extraction around a fixed needle, not orientation-dependent granular separation.

comparisons.objective: Fit and center a gasket between pipe flanges and insert four bolts; unlike separating finishing media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Thin-part insertion into a constrained flange gap and repeated bolt alignment versus controlled pouring, agitation, and selective screen passage.
comparisons.success_condition: Full score requires a centered gasket, four seated bolts, unchanged upper flange, release, and dwell; candidate requires complete feed, at least 98% media recovery, total washer retention, and no spill. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Both involve apertures and alignment, but the tested abilities are constrained assembly versus bulk physical separation.

comparisons.objective: Swipe a magnetic-stripe card through a reader once and return it to a stand; unlike screening a mixed batch.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orienting a thin card and maintaining constrained one-direction speed through a narrow slot versus bimanual load sharing and agitation-driven granular flow.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires a good one-pass read within speed, direction, stripe-orientation, and slot-height limits, followed by stand replacement; no mass recovery or retained-workpiece condition. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: The common idea of passing an object through an opening is generic; controlled swipe trajectory is not selective screening.

comparisons.objective: Connect and lock a hose quick-connect fitting; unlike separating media from finished parts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual collar retraction, coaxial insertion, and latch engagement against hose compliance versus pouring and clearing orientation-dependent screen bridges.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires seated pawl engagement, collar return, stable release, and pull retention; candidate instead grades recovered media mass, washer retention, spill avoidance, screen support, and release dwell. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: It tests compliant connector mating and latching, not bulk separation.

comparisons.objective: Replace two shelf-edge price tickets and discard the old tickets; unlike recovering finishing media.
comparisons.physical_skill: Extracting and inserting thin cards behind a sprung clear strip while preserving neighboring items versus controlled bulk pouring and screen agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires correct old-ticket disposal, correct new-ticket seating, closed strip, untouched reference ticket, release, and long dwell; no granular recovery metric. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: The task is thin-sheet replacement in a channel, not selective passage of mixed rigid bodies.

comparisons.objective: Operate a handheld 3D scanner to cover a cast housing surface; unlike physical media separation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Button actuation, viewpoint planning, standoff/orientation control, turntable coordination, and tracking preservation versus rim grasping, pouring, and bridge clearing.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires 95% scan coverage including the top, clearance, and no part disturbance or scanner contact; candidate requires physical recovery and retention without spill. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: It evaluates sensor trajectory and coverage rather than material handling and separation.

comparisons.objective: Remove individual cooked gnocchi after they float, plate them, and turn off the burner; unlike separating dry ceramic media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed visual/state selection and slotted-spoon scooping from simulated water versus pouring a whole dry mixture and mobilizing bridged elongated media through a screen.
comparisons.success_condition: Credits pieces removed within 45 seconds of floating, plated without hand contact, plus burner shutdown; candidate uses mass recovery, complete feed, washer retention, zero spill, supported-screen release, and dwell. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Although both use perforated tools to retain one material while another passes, gnocchi tests timed individual retrieval from liquid; the candidate tests orientation-dependent dry batch screening and bridge release.

comparisons.objective: Release a drill battery and place it in a tray; unlike screening finishing media.
comparisons.physical_skill: Simultaneous button compression, tool stabilization, and rail-guided extraction versus bimanual pouring, sifting, and granular-flow control.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires both buttons pressed, pack displaced from its seat, tray placement, drill-position preservation, release, and dwell; no separation or recovery requirement. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: It tests interlocked component removal, not mixture separation.

comparisons.objective: Safely assemble a grinding wheel stack on a grinder spindle; unlike screening media from parts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Ordered coaxial placement, thread tightening with torque control, and clamp validation versus controlled pouring and agitation of free bodies.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires the good wheel and stack components correctly seated, safe torque, nut engagement, spin and pull retention tests, and rejects the damaged wheel; candidate requires media recovery and washer retention. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: It evaluates safety-critical rotating-tool assembly and force control, not granular sorting.

comparisons.objective: Carry an untaped-bottom carton of cans to a shelf without losing cans; unlike separating media from retained washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous underside support of articulated bottom flaps during lifting and transport versus pouring into a screen, bimanual sifting, and orientation-dependent bridge release.
comparisons.success_condition: Any can leaving the carton zeros the trial; full score needs shelf placement, uprightness, release, and one-second dwell. Candidate instead intentionally passes media through apertures, retains washers, requires at least 98% recovery, no spill, supported-screen placement, and three-second dwell. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Both demand content preservation and careful bimanual handling, but one tests supporting a failing container while the other tests selective granular separation.

comparisons.objective: Test two light curtains at multiple heights and tag the failed machine; unlike screening a mixed finishing batch.
comparisons.physical_skill: Probe placement through sensing fields, observing functional response, comparative diagnosis, and tag insertion versus pouring and physical particle separation.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires bottom/middle/top rod passes for both fields, correct failed-machine tagging, rod removal, release, and dwell; no recovery, retention, or spill metric. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: It tests inspection and fault-dependent labeling rather than manipulation-driven separation.

comparisons.objective: Roll puff pastry into an even 3 mm sheet; unlike separating rigid finishing media from metal parts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual rolling-pin leveling and distributed deformation control versus granular pouring, agitation, and stable screen placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires sheet length, 2.5–3.5 mm thickness coverage, evenness, and pin set-down; candidate requires recovered mass, retained washers, no contamination or loss, and release dwell. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: It is deformable thickness control, not rigid-body batch separation.

comparisons.objective: Fill three drywall nail holes with spackle and strike them flush; unlike dry-media screening.
comparisons.physical_skill: Loading and angling a putty knife, packing viscous material, and flush surface finishing versus bimanual screen handling and granular-flow control.
comparisons.success_condition: Grades filled-hole depth, limited proud area, avoided face damage, knife set-down, and dwell; no selective passage or mass-recovery criterion. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: It tests tool-mediated surface filling and finishing, not sorting or recovery of rigid components.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates ceramic finishing media from metal washers through a screen; record lays sterile instruments on a contamination-controlled field.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests bimanual screen handling, granular flow, orientation-dependent passage and bridge clearing; record tests individual pick-place and sterile-boundary avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires ≥98% media recovery, every washer retained, no loss/contamination/damage, and released 3 s support dwell; record requires four sterile instruments flat and separated on the field with latched contamination penalties and 1 s clearance dwell.
comparisons.reason: Material classification through physical apertures is meaningfully different from contamination-safe instrument placement. No material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate screens finishing media from washers; record serves a drink through a self-closing drive-thru window.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests controlled granular sifting and bridge release with a bimanually held screen; record tests holding a loaded slider while transferring an upright cup through an opening.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades recovered media mass, washer retention, spill avoidance and released screen seating; record grades cup placement, arm withdrawal and unobstructed window closure, with touch/tip/crush failures.
comparisons.reason: The shared bimanual load-sharing primitive does not make window-and-cup coordination equivalent to aperture-based separation.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates mixed rigid bodies by screening; record unfolds and configures a laptop stand.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests granular-flow control and clearing orientation-dependent bridges; record tests articulated linkage spreading and seating two support rods into slots.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires mass recovery and selective retention without spill; record requires full spread, two rods in the highest slots, contained stable placement and release.
comparisons.reason: Repeated insertion and articulated configuration test a different ability from selective particle passage through a screen.

comparisons.objective: Candidate recovers finishing media while retaining washers; record secures a housing in a rollover fixture, inverts it, locks it and fits a pad.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests bimanual screen motion and granular separation; record tests fixture loading, sliding retention, crank rotation, bolt locking and pad insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate uses recovery ratio, retention, loss and support dwell; record uses sequential physical fixture states with unsafe inversion and loss gates.
comparisons.reason: Fixture retention and indexed inversion are not tested by the candidate, while the record does not test classification or granular flow.

comparisons.objective: Candidate dry-screens ceramic media from metal washers; record prunes a dead rose cane while retaining and binning the cutting.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests screen grasping, pouring, agitation and bridge clearing; record tests tool-mediated cutting, coordinated cutting retention and disposal.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires ≥98% media recovery and all washers retained without spill; record requires a correctly located cut, intact bud, no dropped cutting, binning and safe tool release.
comparisons.reason: Cutting at a biological feature while controlling the freed workpiece is materially different from size/orientation-based screening.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates finishing media from washers; record takes a tympanic temperature on a manikin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests granular flow and bounded agitation; record tests precise probe alignment/insertion, button actuation and submillimetric steadiness during measurement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades recovery mass, retention and spill-free released placement; record requires valid seated measurement, a 3 s motion-bounded hold, safe depth and final thermometer release.
comparisons.reason: Probe seating and measurement stability test fine insertion and hold control, not bulk rigid-body separation.

comparisons.objective: Candidate screens dry finishing media from parts; record clears a washbasin blockage and restores drainage.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests orientation-dependent rigid-particle passage through open mesh; record tests plunger sealing/actuation and hydraulic blockage displacement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires ≥98% receiver-contained media with washers retained and no spill; record requires specified drained-water volume, a clear pipe bore and plunger clearance, with damage/leak gates.
comparisons.reason: Both involve flow, but one tests dry size separation of free rigid bodies and the other tests hydraulic obstruction removal.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates ceramic media from finished washers; record refits and verifies a bakery mixer beater and guard.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests bimanual screen handling and granular bridge release; record tests slotted-hub alignment, push-turn retention, guard placement, bowl lift and guarded powered verification.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades recovery, retention, spill and released support dwell; record requires retained assemblies, guarded operation at specified speeds, stop verification and hand clearance.
comparisons.reason: Mechanical keyed attachment and guarded machine operation are different tested abilities from screening.

comparisons.objective: Candidate classifies a mixed batch by passing media through apertures while retaining washers; record levels a sand bed with a screed riding on rails.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests selective granular passage, orientation-dependent bridging and controlled agitation; record tests maintaining two-rail contact while shaving and redistributing a deformable granular surface.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate measures receiver recovery mass and retained workpieces with immutable spill/loss; record measures bed depth uniformity, bridged pull, surface disturbance, board stowage and release.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest shared granular-material primitive, but selective aperture flow and bridge clearing are meaningfully different from producing a flat graded surface.

comparisons.objective: Candidate screens finishing media from washers; record strips 10 mm of insulation from a cable in a lever station.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests pouring and bimanual agitation of a loaded screen; record tests cable insertion, coordinated lever holding and axial extraction against blade retention.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires recovered media mass, washer retention and spill-free screen release; record requires an 8–12 mm strip, lever release and hand clearance.
comparisons.reason: Coordinated cutting and axial extraction do not test granular classification.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates ceramic media from finished washers; record calibrates a colorimeter and measures a sealed sample.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests load sharing and granular-flow control; record tests reference-dependent cuvette selection, oriented insertion, lid/button operation and instrument workflow.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades physical separation yield and retained parts; record requires a valid calibrated reading at the requested wavelength and both cuvettes returned, released and still.
comparisons.reason: Instrument calibration and reference-dependent measurement are unrelated to physical screening despite both handling multiple small objects.

comparisons.objective: Candidate screens finishing media from washers; record trims a card to length on a guillotine cutter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests bimanual screen manipulation and particle-flow control; record tests card alignment, guarded restraint and blade-handle actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires ≥98% recovery, washer retention and no spill; record requires an 80 mm cut, card alignment, blade-down state and strict hand exclusion from the hazard zone.
comparisons.reason: Precision cutting with hazard-zone control tests a different ability from separation through mesh apertures.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates dry finishing media from metal parts; record loads a caulking gun and seals a bath joint.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests granular sifting and bridge release; record tests release-lever/rod coordination, cartridge loading and controlled sealant deposition along a joint.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate measures recovered mass, retained washers and loss-free released seating; record measures sealed coverage, gap continuity, off-joint mess and final gun placement.
comparisons.reason: Cartridge mechanism operation and continuous material deposition do not overlap meaningfully with dry screening.

comparisons.objective: Candidate screens media from finished washers; record measures subfloor flatness and reports PASS or FAIL.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests tool-driven particle classification; record tests straightedge placement, wedge insertion at the deepest gap and measurement-based classification.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires physical batch separation and quantitative recovery; record requires correct straightedge reference, deepest-gap reading and correct tag placement.
