comparisons.reason: Both end in classification, but the record classifies a surface from a measurement while the candidate physically separates mixed objects.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates ceramic finishing media from washers; record spikes an IV bag and primes its drip chamber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests bimanual screen grasping, pouring and agitation; record tests aseptic cap removal, precise spike insertion and controlled chamber squeeze/release.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades recovery yield, part retention and spill-free support dwell; record requires uncontaminated interfaces, 23–25 mm spike seating, specified liquid height and safe release.
comparisons.reason: Aseptic insertion and fluid priming are meaningfully different from rigid granular separation.

comparisons.objective: Candidate recovers finishing media while retaining reusable metal workpieces; record removes sharps from a reusable surgical tray while retaining blunt instruments and staging the tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests bulk pouring, bimanual screening and orientation-dependent bridge clearing; record tests selective individual grasping, complete-device disposal and tray transport.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires ≥98% media recovery through the screen, every washer retained, no spill/contamination and released dwell; record requires two syringe/needle devices in a sharps bin, blunt instruments retained and tray placed and released in a target area.
comparisons.reason: Both retain one class while relocating another, but the record tests semantic object-by-object segregation; the candidate tests physical size/orientation separation through apertures.

comparisons.objective: Load washable blender jug and lid into a dishwasher while excluding the motor base; candidate separates ceramic media from metal washers through a screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: Selective rigid-object pick-and-place into a rack versus pouring, bimanual screen control, orientation-dependent passage and bridge clearing.
comparisons.success_condition: Jug/lid supported and released in rack for 1 s, with any motor entry vetoed; candidate requires all mixture loaded, ≥98% media recovered, every washer retained, no loss/contamination, and released support dwell for 3 s.
comparisons.reason: Selection and dishwasher placement do not test granular screening or aperture-mediated separation.

comparisons.objective: Press a spring cord lock while threading a shock cord; candidate screens finishing media from retained washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained button force plus deformable-cord insertion versus bulk pouring and controlled agitation of a bimanually held perforated tool.
comparisons.success_condition: Cord passes through with ≥40 mm on each side and spring-grips after release; candidate requires ≥98% receiver recovery with all washers retained and no spill.
comparisons.reason: Both involve passage through an opening, but the tested mechanics—force-gated cord threading versus orientation-dependent granular separation—are meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Seat a Mini-ITX motherboard on four locating pins with rear I/O aligned; candidate separates media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual rigid-board alignment and simultaneous multi-pin insertion versus pouring, screen load sharing and bridge-clearing agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: All holes seated on pins, I/O aligned, board still and grippers ≥60 mm clear for 1 s; candidate grades mass recovery, washer retention, immutable loss and a 3 s released dwell.
comparisons.reason: Precision fixture insertion does not test granular flow through apertures.

comparisons.objective: Extract exactly one nested paper cup through a dispenser gasket and stand it on a mat; candidate performs dry media/part screening.
comparisons.physical_skill: Compliant single-item extraction without crushing or releasing extra cups versus controlled pouring and bimanual granular-flow control.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly one undamaged cup upright, released and wholly on the mat; candidate requires complete loading, ≥98% media recovery, retained washers and no spill or contamination.
comparisons.reason: The cup task tests compliant extraction and singulation, not sieve-mediated material separation.

comparisons.objective: Refit a loaded drawer on roller slides, close it, then pull-test it; candidate screens media from parts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual drawer carrying, hook/roller clearance alignment and sliding versus pouring and agitation of a perforated screen.
comparisons.success_condition: Drawer must be on its slides, previously closed hands-off, then open 30–80 mm with load retained; candidate succeeds by mass recovery, washer retention and released support dwell.
comparisons.reason: Shared load retention and bimanual handling are generic; the tested engagement and flow abilities differ.

comparisons.objective: Mount a shaft between bench centres using a tailstock release lever; candidate separates finishing media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a spring-loaded lever while seating two conical centre holes versus bimanual screen manipulation and orientation-dependent particle passage.
comparisons.success_condition: Both points seated, lever at rest, hands clear and shaft still; candidate requires ≥98% recovered media, every washer retained and no loss.
comparisons.reason: Spring-controlled shaft alignment is unrelated to granular screening despite both requiring coordinated hands.

comparisons.objective: Insert both air-shroud tabs under a server fan cage and lower the shroud into its seat; candidate screens finishing media.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual large-panel tilt, dual-tab insertion and constrained lowering versus pouring, load sharing and bridge-clearing screen motion.
comparisons.success_condition: Both tabs inserted, four corners seated, released and still for 1 s; candidate uses recovery fraction, retention, spill vetoes and a 3 s released dwell.
comparisons.reason: The shroud task tests constrained insertion and seating, not size/orientation separation through a mesh.

comparisons.objective: Lock a fallen seesaw platform with a pin before placing two blocks; candidate screens media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Platform leveling, aligned safety-pin insertion and subsequent block placement versus controlled bulk loading and bimanual sifting.
comparisons.success_condition: Pin locks all hinge layers before loading, blocks rest on marks, platform level and arms clear for 3 s; candidate requires media recovery and washer retention without spill.
comparisons.reason: The central tested ability is safety interlocking before loading, not particulate separation.

comparisons.objective: Open a locker supporting a leaning case and remove the case upright without dropping it; candidate performs screen separation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Door/case coordination and upright transport of a precarious load versus screen grasping, pouring and granular agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Case never tips beyond 45° or drops, then stands released on the mat; candidate grades recovered media mass, retained washers and immutable loss.
comparisons.reason: Precarious rigid-object extraction is physically different from aperture-mediated sifting.

comparisons.objective: Secure a loose needle in a sharps container before discarding its tray and forceps; candidate screens media from metal parts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hazard-aware tool handling and ordered waste placement versus controlled pouring and bimanual granular separation.
comparisons.success_condition: Needle safely contained, tray/forceps binned, released and still, with needle-touch and improper disposal vetoes; candidate requires ≥98% media recovery and washer retention.
comparisons.reason: The sharps task tests safe sequencing and avoidance of a hazardous point, not granular flow.

comparisons.objective: Empty four concentrate bottles into a filling tank and close its inlet valve at the target level; candidate separates dry media and washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated liquid pouring plus timing a valve closure versus pouring a rigid mixture and mobilizing orientation-dependent media through a screen.
comparisons.success_condition: All bottles emptied, valve shut, level within 12.5–13.5 cm, with overflow/spill vetoes; candidate requires ≥98% solid-media recovery and all washers retained.
comparisons.reason: Both include pouring and spill control, but liquid batching/valve timing does not test selective passage, bridging or retained workpieces.

comparisons.objective: Remove a screwdriver, latch a control box and switch its supply on safely; candidate screens finishing media.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool extraction, cover closure/latching and rocker actuation versus bimanual screen handling and granular-flow control.
comparisons.success_condition: Tool released on table, cover latched shut, supply on and arms clear, with unsafe energization vetoed; candidate grades loading and media recovery with loss/contamination vetoes.
comparisons.reason: Electrical closeout sequencing is unrelated to physical screening.

comparisons.objective: Insert a rolled poster into a mailing tube and press caps into both ends; candidate separates media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Long-object coaxial insertion and two interference-fit cap insertions versus pouring and bridge-clearing through screen apertures.
comparisons.success_condition: Roll at least 15 mm inside both ends, both caps aligned/seated, all parts released and still; candidate requires mass-based media recovery and washer retention.
comparisons.reason: The mailing task tests coaxial packaging insertion rather than granular size/orientation separation.

comparisons.objective: Lift a loaded fry basket and hang its hook on the fryer hanger without losing fries; candidate screens ceramic media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Long-handle lifting, level load transport and hook placement versus bimanual rim grasping, pouring and controlled screen agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Basket hangs by its hook above the liquid with all fries retained and robot clear for 1 s; candidate requires media to pass through while washers remain, with ≥98% recovery and 3 s support dwell.
comparisons.reason: Both retain loose contents, but hanging an intact loaded basket does not test selective aperture passage or bridge release.

comparisons.objective: Crank an insulation tester while probing three cable cores and identify the leaking core; candidate performs mechanical screening.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous rotary actuation coordinated with precise probing and instrument interpretation versus pouring and screen agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: All cores tested under sufficient crank speed, only the leaking core flagged, probe returned and hands clear; candidate grades recovered media mass and retained washers.
comparisons.reason: Diagnostic measurement and hidden-fault identification are unrelated to granular separation.

comparisons.objective: Move a granite mortar and leave its loose pestle contained inside; candidate screens media from metal washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Heavy vessel transport and placement while managing one loose rigid object versus pouring many bodies and selectively passing media through apertures.
comparisons.success_condition: Mortar upright in target, pestle geometrically contained, both stable and robot clear; candidate requires media to leave the screen while every washer remains.
comparisons.reason: Shared containment is generic; the mortar task preserves all objects together and has no separation or flow requirement.

comparisons.objective: Seat an access panel and place two retainer bars into rib slots; candidate performs dry media screening.
comparisons.physical_skill: Planar panel alignment followed by two constrained bar placements versus bimanual tool motion and orientation-dependent granular passage.
comparisons.success_condition: Panel flush and both bars flat, aligned and overlapping the panel by ≥20 mm; candidate uses mass recovery, washer retention and released dwell. The simulation rubric does not distinguish a motionless still-gripped part, but this omission does not create duplication.
comparisons.reason: Panel closeout is a multi-part alignment task, not material separation.

comparisons.objective: Load four connector modules into a spring-open hinged frame and squeeze it shut until it clicks; candidate screens media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated narrow-support placement while preserving neighboring modules, followed by spring-frame closure versus pouring and controlled agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: All four modules seated, frame clicked shut and hands ≥3 cm clear for 1 s; candidate requires ≥98% recovered media, every washer retained and no spill.
comparisons.reason: The frame task tests cumulative insertion and latching rather than granular flow through a mesh.

comparisons.objective: Unlock a jigsaw shoe, set a 45° bevel, relock it and release the saw; candidate separates media and washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Articulated-tool adjustment and clamp actuation versus bimanual screen support, pouring and bridge clearing.
comparisons.success_condition: Shoe at 45±2°, clamped, still and hands clear for 2 s, with drop/loss vetoes; candidate succeeds through recovery fraction, retention and 3 s released support dwell.
comparisons.reason: Angle setting and locking do not test granular separation.

comparisons.objective: Verify a seat-belt retractor locks after slow payout and a jerk, then guide it home; candidate screens finishing media.
comparisons.physical_skill: Velocity-profile control, force loading of an inertia lock and guided retraction versus pouring and bounded agitation of a loaded screen.
comparisons.success_condition: Slow payout ≥120 mm, jerk-lock within 25 mm, ≥6 N hold, then slow return and released dwell; candidate requires ≥98% media recovery and washer retention.
comparisons.reason: The seat-belt task tests dynamic lock response and controlled webbing motion, not screening.

comparisons.objective: Hook a laryngoscope blade onto a handle and swing it into its lit detent; candidate separates finishing media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small hinge-bar engagement, regrasping and rotational latching versus bimanual screen manipulation and granular-flow control.
comparisons.success_condition: Blade hooked, swung to 90°, lit/clicked, scope released on tray and still for 1 s; candidate requires complete loading, ≥98% recovery, all washers retained and no loss. The task declares a pose-constrained hinge effect, but its rubric remains clear.
comparisons.reason: Hook-and-detent assembly is physically different from selective aperture passage and bridge clearing.

comparisons.objective: Seal, shake, reopen, and upright a cocktail shaker without losing contents; candidate screens finishing media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both use bimanual agitation and spill control, but this record tests press-fit sealing, axial mixing strokes, and reopening rather than orientation-selective passage through apertures and bridge clearing.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires sealed shaking/mixing, retained beads or liquid, reopening, and an upright tin; candidate requires complete feed, >=98% media recovery, every washer retained, reseated screen, clearance, and 3 s dwell.
comparisons.reason: Agitation is a shared primitive, but the tested physical outcome is sealed mixing versus selective granular separation. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Open a bottle by lowering a detented safety loop and pressing a rocker while keeping it upright.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential latch manipulation and bottle stabilization, not pouring, granular screening, bridge release, or bimanual screen handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Credit tracks safety-loop and lid angles with upright/support and force fault gates; candidate tracks feed fraction, recovered-media mass, washer retention, loss, damage, release, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: The record tests a passive detent-and-rocker mechanism, meaningfully unrelated to selective separation. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Mix flour and liquid into dough with a spoon while steadying a loose bowl.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool-mediated stirring and bowl stabilization of a wet mixture, not pouring a dry mixture through apertures or clearing orientation-dependent media bridges.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores mixed-in flour share, with zero for excessive bowl tilt or material loss; candidate scores screened media recovery and washer retention with immutable spill/loss rules.
comparisons.reason: Although a sieve appears in real-world post-trial measurement, the robot's tested ability is dough mixing, not screening. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Magnetically seat and release a stylus, then lift a thin tablet while the stylus remains attached.
comparisons.physical_skill: Magnetic-face alignment, thin-object pickup, and unsupported carrying rather than granular pouring, sifting, and bridge clearing.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires correct stylus seating/release followed by all tablet corners held 50 mm up for 5 s; candidate requires >=98% media recovery, washer retention, screen placement, clearance, and 3 s dwell.
comparisons.reason: The tested attachment-and-carry ability is unrelated to material separation. The spec defers numeric seating tolerances and detailed support rules to its README, but that omission does not create plausible overlap.

comparisons.objective: Roll and hold a limp training forearm to expose a wristband, scan it, then restore the arm and scanner.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual limb support plus scanner aiming/triggering within an optical envelope, not dry-mixture flow control or screen agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires a valid timed barcode read, gentle forearm motion, and final restoration; candidate requires mass recovery, absolute washer retention, no contamination/loss, screen release, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: This tests constrained sensing while maintaining a sprung limb pose, not physical sorting. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Dry-fit and glue a broken mug handle, then align, press, and release the joint.
comparisons.physical_skill: Precision mating of two fracture faces, controlled adhesive dispensing, and force application rather than screening and granular-flow management.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires dry fit, 10–30 uL beads on both faces, tight pose tolerances, >=3 N pressing, clean placement, and released stability; candidate uses recovery mass and retained-washer outcomes.
comparisons.reason: The record tests adhesive repair and precision seating, a different ability from selective separation. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Uncork a wine bottle while it remains in its cradle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Corkscrew tip alignment, helical insertion, stabilization, and axial extraction rather than pouring and orientation-selective screening.
comparisons.success_condition: Full credit requires the cork out and away while the bottle remains within cradle displacement/rotation bounds; candidate requires media recovery and zero washer escape or receiver contamination.
comparisons.reason: Rotary insertion and cork extraction are meaningfully different from dry-media separation. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Use a pendant hoist and a guiding hand to land a motor over four base studs and leave the chain slack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated suspended-load control and multi-stud alignment under pinch/strike hazards, not granular flow or sieve manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires four studs through, feet flat, bounded chain slack, release, stillness, and no under-load, pinch, or fast-strike event; candidate grades recovery mass, washer retention, and spill-free screen release.
comparisons.reason: This tests safe placement of a hoisted rigid load, clearly unrelated to screening. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Cinch a loaded flexible bin liner, remove it, and release it beside the bin without spilling.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable drawstring closure and bag extraction; candidate instead uses rigid screen handling and orientation-dependent passage of many rigid bodies.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires bounded bag opening, retained contents, clearance from the bin, released tabletop placement, gripper clearance, and 2 s stability; candidate requires >=98% media recovered while every washer remains in the screen.
comparisons.reason: Both penalize spills and include release, but bag cinching/extraction and aperture-based material separation test different abilities. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Depress an autofolder feed table, insert and square a newsletter stack to a retarder stop, then release it under the feed wheel.
comparisons.physical_skill: Compliant table depression and planar stack insertion/alignment into a nip, not pouring or selectively passing granular bodies through apertures.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires millimetric stack position/yaw/gap, table release and clamping, stable housing, clearance, and 1 s rest; candidate requires feed completion, media recovery, washer retention, and no loss.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is loading and clamping a sheet stack, not screening. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Install an overlength U-joint cross through a yoke by inserting one journal, swinging it level, and centering both journals.
comparisons.physical_skill: Constrained rigid-part insertion, pivoting, and bilateral hole alignment rather than granular pouring and bridge-clearing agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires both journals inserted to specified depths, centered/aligned within tolerances, and still for 1 s; candidate is judged by separated mass fractions and retained washers.
comparisons.reason: This is a geometric assembly insertion task, materially different from selective screening. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Tighten a tourniquet windlass to the green pressure range and lock the rod in its clip.
comparisons.physical_skill: Torque against elastic backdrive followed by snap-latching, not screen grasping, granular-flow orientation, or bridge release.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires >=250 mmHg, a mechanically locked rod, and 1 s hands-clear state; candidate requires screened recovery, retention, placement, and 3 s dwell.
comparisons.reason: The record tests tensioning and latch capture, not separation. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Create a sound TIG weld along an L-shaped seam using a torch and filler rod.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual thermal process control, torch travel, and filler dabbing rather than dry-material handling and screening.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores sound 5 mm weld segments using bead coverage and defect limits, followed by tool return and clearance; candidate scores material recovery and prohibits spill, contamination, and washer loss.
comparisons.reason: Weld formation is entirely different from orientation-selective particle passage. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Clip a spring-hinged pulse oximeter onto a manikin index finger while steadying the hand.
comparisons.physical_skill: Opening a spring clip, insertion over soft-body geometry, and gentle stabilization rather than granular screening.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires adequate fingertip insertion, jaw closure, display orientation, release, stillness, and no excessive hand displacement or dropped device; candidate requires mass separation and screen release.
comparisons.reason: This tests gentle clip placement on a patient surrogate, not sorting. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Seat a loose rack on a pinion so a parallel gripper's fingers open evenly.
comparisons.physical_skill: Gear-tooth meshing, rack alignment, and functional transmission verification rather than granular-flow and sieve manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires seated racks, bounded jaw-center error, both fingers opening at least 15 mm, stillness, and gripper clearance; candidate requires media recovery and washer retention.
comparisons.reason: The record tests precision mechanism assembly and coupled motion. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Cut copper tubing at a mark with a screw-feed tubing cutter without denting it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Alternating cutter revolution and controlled screw-feed force, not pouring or aperture-based sorting.
comparisons.success_condition: Credit tracks groove/cut progress and location, with permanent zero for excessive bite or measurable tube denting, plus final gripper clearance; candidate tracks recovered media and retained washers.
comparisons.reason: Controlled rotary cutting is meaningfully unrelated to media screening. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Uniformly heat-shrink a sleeve over a cable lug, then return and switch off the heat gun.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual cable rotation and spatially uniform noncontact heating, not dry granular flow or bridge clearing.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores recovered sleeve stations/sides while rejecting nozzle contact, overheating, charring, or dropped equipment; candidate requires >=98% screened-media recovery without loss or contamination.
comparisons.reason: The tested thermal-processing ability differs fundamentally from selective separation. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Separate keyed-pivot kitchen shears into two halves and leave them safely in a washing tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Keyed-joint orientation, axial disassembly, and handle-only manipulation rather than screen agitation and granular sorting.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires separated, supported, stationary halves with hand clearance; metal contact, fracture, or deformation permanently fails the trial. Candidate instead requires mass recovery and washer retention.
comparisons.reason: This tests constrained disassembly through a keyed pivot, not screening. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Place a screwdriver in the right tool-chest drawer while the adjacent drawer remains open.
comparisons.physical_skill: Drawer manipulation, obstacle-aware tool placement, and chest stabilization rather than granular pouring and sifting.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires the screwdriver wholly inside the target drawer with specified drawer states and no chest tip, drag, or off-table event; candidate requires selective recovery and screen placement.
comparisons.reason: Tool storage amid an open-drawer obstruction is a different tested ability. No material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Open a robot-vacuum brush door by releasing its catch; candidate separates finishing media from washers through a screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: Simultaneous button squeeze and hinged-door lifting versus bimanual pouring, screen agitation, granular-flow control, and reseating.
comparisons.success_condition: Door ≥80° open, vacuum stable, hands clear for 1 s versus ≥98% media recovery, every washer retained, no loss/damage, screen released for 3 s.
comparisons.reason: The tested mechanism and outcome are unrelated; no material rubric details needed for comparison are missing.

comparisons.objective: Insert five coins through a piggy-bank slot; candidate selectively screens ceramic media while retaining washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Thin-object pickup, reorientation, and one-at-a-time slot insertion versus bulk pouring and orientation-dependent many-body passage through apertures.
comparisons.success_condition: All five coins wholly inside without tipping the bank versus recovery-mass threshold, complete washer retention, immutable spill controls, and released screen dwell.
comparisons.reason: Both involve objects passing openings, but insertion alignment of individual coins does not test selective granular separation or bridge clearing.

comparisons.objective: Force a straw through a lidded cup’s X-slot to depth; candidate separates a dry parts/media mixture with a screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: Axial insertion through compliant flaps with controlled force versus bimanual screen handling and agitation-driven granular flow.
comparisons.success_condition: Straw through the slot and within 20 mm of the cup bottom, released and still versus ≥98% media recovered with all washers retained and no spill/damage.
comparisons.reason: Shared use of a physical opening is generic; the candidate tests selective many-body flow rather than forceful single-part insertion.

comparisons.objective: Relocate a hot iron to a safe part of an ironing mat; candidate recovers finishing media from metal parts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safe grasping, transport, and upright placement of one hazardous appliance versus coordinated pouring, sifting, bridge clearing, and screen placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Iron upright in the right-hand zone without soleplate contact or dropping versus mass-based media recovery, washer retention, no contamination/loss, and 3 s released dwell.
comparisons.reason: The objectives, physical interactions, and graded hazards are meaningfully different; the recovered board rubric is sufficiently detailed.

comparisons.objective: Replace a toilet roll and reinstall its spring spindle; candidate screens media from finished washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Axial threading and two-end socket seating of a sprung spindle versus bimanual granular separation through apertures.
comparisons.success_condition: New roll on spindle, both tips seated, empty tube removed, hands clear versus ≥98% media recovered and all washers retained with the screen safely reseated.
comparisons.reason: This is constrained assembly and seating, not selective particle flow or agitation.

comparisons.objective: Mix layered liquid in two open test tubes without spilling; candidate separates dry ceramic media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled tube agitation for liquid mixing and reracking versus bimanual screen agitation that reorients rigid media to clear bridges while retaining larger parts.
comparisons.success_condition: Both tubes mixed, unspilled, racked, and released for 1 s versus ≥98% media in the receiver, all washers in the screen, no spill/damage, and 3 s released dwell.
comparisons.reason: Agitation and spill avoidance overlap, but the tested abilities differ materially: liquid homogenization versus aperture-selective granular separation and bridge clearing.

comparisons.objective: Fit and latch a phone into a hybrid case; candidate separates finishing media from workpieces.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rigid-part orientation, compliant-lip alignment, and sequential corner snapping versus load-shared screen manipulation and granular-flow control.
comparisons.success_condition: Phone correctly oriented with all four corners seated, released and still versus recovery fraction, complete washer retention, loss/damage constraints, and screen dwell.
comparisons.reason: Compliant enclosure assembly does not test bulk material separation.

comparisons.objective: Carry a full cup safely past a laptop to a coaster; candidate screens a dry industrial mixture.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stable liquid-container transport and obstacle clearance versus controlled feed pouring, bimanual sifting, and orientation-dependent particle passage.
comparisons.success_condition: Cup upright on coaster with no spill, laptop contact, or unsafe proximity versus ≥98% media recovery with retained washers and no rim/floor loss.
comparisons.reason: Although both penalize spilling, safe transport of one container is not granular separation.

comparisons.objective: Air-test a handhole before conditionally removing its cover bolts; candidate separates finishing media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed probe placement, condition-dependent restraint, and bolt removal versus bimanual screen handling and granular bridge clearing.
comparisons.success_condition: Valid continuous 60 s sample followed by alarm-dependent bolt/cover outcome versus mass recovery, washer retention, no loss/damage, and released screen dwell.
comparisons.reason: The handhole task tests safety sequencing and fastener manipulation, not selective material flow.

comparisons.objective: Clamp a metal plate and drill through its marked point safely; candidate screens ceramic media from metal washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fixture tightening, drill-press operation, forceful cutting, and hazard clearance versus controlled pouring and agitation of free rigid bodies.
comparisons.success_condition: Clamped plate drilled through on mark, no unsafe proximity, drill left safe versus ≥98% media recovered, every washer retained, and screen reseated without loss.
comparisons.reason: Machining and workholding have no meaningful tested-ability overlap with sifting.

comparisons.objective: Fit and hand-tighten an oxygen regulator on a cylinder valve; candidate separates media from finished parts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Yoke alignment, pin insertion, gasket seating, and screw tightening versus bimanual pouring, agitation, and aperture-mediated flow.
comparisons.success_condition: Regulator seated, aligned, torque-qualified, released and still without drop/tip events versus media recovery and washer-retention thresholds with no spill/damage.
comparisons.reason: Precision mechanical installation is distinct from bulk dry separation.

comparisons.objective: Open a can using a hand-held rotary opener; candidate screens finishing media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain a clamp while coordinating continuous key rotation around a rim versus coordinated screen grasping and bridge-clearing agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Lid fully cut, opener removed, can upright and released versus ≥98% recovery, all washers retained, no loss or damage, and screen released on supports.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual coordination is generic; cutting a continuous seam does not test granular separation.

comparisons.objective: Mount a filled malt cup on a drink mixer so the spindle and run switch engage; candidate separates dry media and workpieces.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cup transport and constrained hook/guide/spindle seating without spilling versus feed pouring, bimanual screen agitation, and selective passage.
comparisons.success_condition: Cup seated on run step with spindle inside, motor on, released and still versus recovery fraction, washer retention, immutable loss controls, and support dwell.
comparisons.reason: Both handle loaded vessels, but the mixer task tests fixture engagement rather than bulk separation.

comparisons.objective: Load an IV set into a pump module without lifting, stretching, or twisting it; candidate screens rigid finishing media.
comparisons.physical_skill: Ordered fitment and clamp insertion with flexible-tube management versus bimanual rigid-body granular-flow control.
comparisons.success_condition: Fitment seated first, clamp home, tubing unstretched/untwisted, hands clear for 2 s versus ≥98% media recovery, washers retained, screen released for 3 s.
comparisons.reason: Flexible medical-set installation is unrelated to selective screening.

comparisons.objective: Install a comb busbar across three breaker terminals; candidate separates finishing media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Multi-pin simultaneous alignment followed by repeated screw tightening versus bimanual pouring, screen agitation, and particle reorientation.
comparisons.success_condition: All pins seated and clamped, pull test passed, tools and hands clear for 2 s versus mass recovery, complete workpiece retention, and loss-free released dwell.
comparisons.reason: Multi-point electrical assembly does not measure granular separation or bridge clearing.

comparisons.objective: Remove a tagged bin from a gravity lane while restraining the following bin; candidate screens media from finished parts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Dynamic interception, temporary restraint, bin extraction, and lane restoration versus bimanual screen manipulation and many-body flow control.
comparisons.success_condition: Tagged bin in tote, next bin moves ≤2 cm, remaining lane closes up versus ≥98% media recovered with every washer retained and no spill/damage.
comparisons.reason: Both manage gravity-driven objects, but bin-flow control and granular aperture separation are materially different abilities.

comparisons.objective: Form a two-bend 45° offset in tubing; candidate separates dry media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool-constrained plastic bending with springback compensation versus pouring and agitation-driven reorientation of free particles.
comparisons.success_condition: Two bends within angular/offset tolerances, tube on template and still versus recovery fraction, washer retention, no loss/damage, and screen support dwell.
comparisons.reason: Tube forming tests deformation and geometry, not selective granular flow.

comparisons.objective: Calibrate a mounted tool tip by making stable contact from four angular poses; candidate screens finishing media.
comparisons.physical_skill: Submillimetre contact positioning and repeated orientation control versus bimanual load sharing, pouring, and bridge-clearing agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Four distinct 1 s contact poses within force, position, lean, and stability limits versus ≥98% recovery with retained washers and a released screen.
comparisons.reason: Contact calibration and granular separation have no meaningful objective or success-condition equivalence.

comparisons.objective: Water soil while moving a leaf aside and avoiding leaf wetting; candidate separates ceramic media from metal washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual occlusion management and controlled liquid pouring versus feed pouring followed by screen grasping, granular agitation, and bridge clearing.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 90 ml reaches soil, at most 10 ml contacts leaves, jug and leaf restored versus ≥98% media recovered, every washer retained, no spill/loss, and screen reseated.
comparisons.reason: Controlled pouring overlaps generically, but the plant task does not test aperture-selective many-body flow or retention of a second material class.

comparisons.objective: Seat a click-type torque wrench on a busbar lug bolt and tighten to the click without over-torque; candidate screens finishing media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Socket-to-hex seating, controlled torque application, and stopping on a one-shot detent cue versus bimanual pouring, orientation-selective screening, and bridge-clearing agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires seated socket, click, 90–110% target torque, no unseated turning or over-torque, release, and 1 s stability. Candidate requires all feed transferred, ≥98% media recovered, every washer retained, no loss/contamination/damage, supported screen release, and 3 s dwell. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Fastener torque control and click-cue response do not test granular separation or selective retention.

comparisons.objective: Release a drawer from two slides and set it flat on the table; candidate separates ceramic media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Opposite-sense latch actuation while pulling and supporting a drawer versus controlled pouring, bimanual screen handling, and bridge-clearing agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Drawer must clear both slides, rest flat and still, and be released with 30 mm hand clearance for 1 s. Candidate instead grades transfer fraction, ≥98% media recovery, total washer retention, absence of spill/damage, supported release, and 3 s dwell. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: The shared need for bimanual load support and final release is generic; the tested mechanisms and outcomes differ.

comparisons.objective: Set a telescoping gauge to a bearing bore diameter and leave it on a stand; candidate screens media from workpieces.
comparisons.physical_skill: Expand and lock a precision gauge against a bore, withdraw without changing span, and place it on a stand versus bulk pouring and orientation-dependent granular screening.
comparisons.success_condition: Gauge span must be within 0.10 mm, tips clear, tool released and still, with full credit for correct stand placement across three lots. Candidate requires ≥98% recovered media, all washers retained, no loss/contamination/damage, and a released 3 s dwell. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Precision internal metrology and locked-span preservation are meaningfully different from separating many free bodies through apertures.

comparisons.objective: Use a detacher to release and withdraw an anti-theft pin from a jacket cuff; candidate separates finishing media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Precisely seat a detacher while coordinating pin extraction against a physical latch versus pouring, two-arm screen control, and agitation that induces end-first media passage.
comparisons.success_condition: Credit depends on detacher seating and 5–15 mm pin travel while seated, ending with the pin out and hands 30 mm clear for 1 s. Candidate requires complete loading, ≥98% media recovery, every washer retained, no spill/contamination/damage, and supported release for 3 s. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Latch release under simultaneous tool placement and extraction does not test granular screening.

comparisons.objective: Open a sealed cocktail shaker with a correctly placed strike, then set both tins upright; candidate screens dry ceramic media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold one tin, deliver a directional impact at the open-side seam, and lift the other tin versus controlled bulk flow, bimanual screen tilting, and bounded agitation to clear bridges.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires seal break by the qualifying blow, tin separation, upright placement, release, and no dent/spill/fall. Candidate requires ≥98% media recovery, all washers retained, no media loss or receiver contamination, no washer damage, and 3 s released support. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Although both penalize spill or damage, impact-mediated seal breaking is not the candidate’s orientation-selective separation ability.

comparisons.objective: Latch a tool-less server rail into the rear and front flanges of the same rack U; candidate separates finishing media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Peg-to-square-hole alignment, latch insertion, telescoping rail extension, and level placement versus pouring and bimanual agitation of a perforated screen.
comparisons.success_condition: Both rail ends must latch at the marked U, remain within 0.5° of level, not fall, and be released for 2 s; partial credit is rear latch only. Candidate instead requires full feed transfer, ≥98% media recovery, washer retention, no loss/damage, and 3 s released support. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Rack-rail alignment and sequential latching test rigid insertion geometry, not granular classification.

comparisons.objective: Align and click a mop frame’s swivelling socket onto its handle; candidate screens media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize a swivel, coaxially insert a long handle, compress a spring button, and latch it versus bimanual pouring, screen tilting, and bridge-clearing agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Handle must insert and click with lug seated and button exposed, remain on the bench and still, and be released for 1 s. Candidate requires ≥98% media recovery, every washer retained, no spill/contamination/damage, and supported release for 3 s. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: A single coaxial insertion-and-latch task is materially different from selective many-body passage through a screen.

comparisons.objective: Heat and solder a copper water joint without burning flux; candidate performs dry mechanical separation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual torch and solder-wire control, thermal timing, precise feeding, and safe tool withdrawal versus granular-flow control and bimanual screen agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires ≥8.1 mm solder fed above liquidus, cooling below solidus, tools safely away, and no burnt flux, trapped wire, misdirected flame, or dropped tool. Candidate grades recovery mass, washer retention, spill/contamination/damage, and released support. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Thermal process control and solder wetting do not overlap meaningfully with mechanical screening.

comparisons.objective: Unfold an attached tablet support and leave the tablet standing in portrait orientation; candidate separates media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manipulate linked passive panels and transfer tablet weight onto a stable support polygon versus pouring, load-shared screen handling, and orientation-dependent granular agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Tablet must stand at 50–70° tilt with bounded roll/facing error, supported only by tablet and stand, hands 30 mm clear, stable for 5 s. Candidate requires ≥98% media recovery, washer retention, no loss/damage, and a 3 s released dwell. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Deploying a linked kickstand and establishing static stability is not granular separation.

comparisons.objective: Select fitting tweezers and peel protective film from a display module while stabilizing its carrier; candidate screens finishing media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool selection by tip fit, tab capture, controlled adhesive peeling, carrier stabilization, and tool replacement versus bimanual pouring and screen agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Grades peeled length to 115 mm, limits carrier motion and premature seam separation, requires film deposited outside the carrier, both tweezers returned, and hands clear for 1 s. Candidate grades mass transfer/recovery, washer retention, spill/contamination/damage, and supported release. No material rubric detail is missing in the recovered board specification.
comparisons.reason: Adhesive peeling with constrained tool selection tests a different ability from aperture-mediated granular sorting.

comparisons.objective: Compress and fit a spring tension rod between cupboard walls at a marked level; candidate separates media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual rod compression, endpoint placement against opposed walls, and controlled release under spring preload versus pouring and agitation of granular contents in a screen.
comparisons.success_condition: Rod must self-support with both caps pressing the walls, lie within the height band and level/square tolerances, remain clear of the table, and hold for 4 s after release. Candidate requires ≥98% media recovery, all washers retained, no loss/damage, and 3 s supported release. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Opposed spring-force installation and geometric placement do not test selective granular passage.

comparisons.objective: Send a loaded tote down a roller conveyor to a far station without a hard impact; candidate screens media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Impart and regulate tote motion remotely while preserving load stability versus close bimanual pouring, tilting, and agitation of a separating screen.
comparisons.success_condition: Tote must stop at the station with upright contained bottle, impact ≤0.40 m/s, no lifting/tipping, robot outside a keep-out zone, and 1 s stillness. Candidate requires complete pouring, ≥98% media recovery, total washer retention, no spill/contamination/damage, and released screen support. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Conveyor transport with momentum and stopping control is not orientation-selective screening.

comparisons.objective: Bleed air from a brake caliper while closing the bleeder before every pedal return; candidate separates dry finishing media.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinate repeated pedal strokes with wrench-controlled valve timing and final closure versus pouring and bimanual granular-flow manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Grades residual air volume, permanently fails on air drawn back in, and requires bleeder shut, pedal returned, tools released, and 1 s final stability. Candidate grades recovered media mass, retained washers, no spill/contamination/damage, and 3 s released support. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Sequenced hydraulic purging and valve timing are materially different from screen-based classification.

comparisons.objective: Align and press a servo horn onto a splined shaft at the zero mark; candidate screens media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine coaxial alignment, discrete spline-index selection, axial press-fit seating, and orientation preservation versus bulk pouring and bridge-clearing screen agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Horn must be on the correct spline within 2°, coaxial, low-tilt and flush within 0.5 mm, then still with hands 30 mm clear for 1 s; wrong final tooth scores zero. Candidate requires ≥98% media recovery, total washer retention, no loss/damage, and 3 s released support. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Precision indexed insertion tests a single rigid mating interface, not selective transport of many bodies through apertures.

comparisons.objective: Adjust a cabinet hinge side screw to equalize reveals, then close the flap door; candidate separates finishing media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Seat and turn a screwdriver in the correct adjustment cam, assess coupled door geometry, close, and release versus bimanual pouring and granular screen agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Door must close with 3–6 mm reveals differing by ≤1 mm, flush within 0.6 mm, still and released for 1 s; excessive sag from loosening the clamp permanently fails. Candidate requires complete transfer, ≥98% media recovery, all washers retained, no spill/contamination/damage, and 3 s released support. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Mechanism adjustment to a measured final alignment is a different tested ability from dry media/workpiece separation.

comparisons.objective: Square a racked gantry by sliding both rail carriages onto their end stops.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual synchronized pushing, load sharing, and binding avoidance on constrained rails.
comparisons.success_condition: Both carriages seated against 0.05 mm stop tolerances, beam stable, and grippers released; earlier versions omit slide-path enforcement, later versions require on-rail travel.
comparisons.reason: No pouring, granular transport, aperture screening, selective retention, or spill-sensitive media recovery.

comparisons.objective: Extend a suitcase handle past an intermediate stop and lock both rails at full height.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain button depression while pulling a telescoping mechanism and stabilizing the case.
comparisons.success_condition: Handle at 520±3 mm with both locks engaged, case retained near its start, and hands clear for 1 second.
comparisons.reason: Tests coordinated latch operation and telescoping extraction, not tool-mediated size separation or granular-flow control.

comparisons.objective: Release a drill bit from an unpowered keyless chuck and place it in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Counterhold a loose drill, twist a chuck sleeve, extract a retained shaft, and place it.
comparisons.success_condition: Bit wholly outside the chuck and stably supported; full credit requires it inside the tray with drill and hands safely released.
comparisons.reason: Tests torque-mediated release and extraction of one retained component, not bulk media passage through apertures.

comparisons.objective: Install a screen protector using a close-fitting alignment tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Level fit-over alignment, pressing to adhere, and lifting the empty tray without disturbing the glass.
comparisons.success_condition: Glass flat and within 1.5 mm of target, tray removed, phone not displaced, and hands clear for 1 second.
comparisons.reason: Tray alignment and adhesion are unrelated to orientation-dependent screening and recovery of free rigid particles.

comparisons.objective: Tighten and fit an already-threaded necktie on a rigid collar form.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated pulling and fitting of a reduced deformable/fixed-topology tie model.
comparisons.success_condition: Released 5-second hold with knot size, position, blade order, twist, and tip-length bounds; damage or unthreading fails.
comparisons.reason: Tests deformable dressing adjustment rather than pouring, bimanual rigid-tool agitation, and particulate separation.

comparisons.objective: Uncap a spray can and coat a plaque while limiting overspray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cap removal, can aiming, controlled spray-path coverage, and overspray management.
comparisons.success_condition: Coverage and overspray bounds govern the result, with the can safely released; versions refine coating measurements.
comparisons.reason: Material application by a spray tool does not test physical sieving, particle bridging, or retention by aperture size.

comparisons.objective: Load a card squarely under a clipboard's spring clip.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a sprung lever open while sliding and aligning a thin sheet to a stop.
comparisons.success_condition: Card retained under the clip, aligned within 2 mm and 2 degrees for full credit, released and stable; retention is pull-tested.
comparisons.reason: Tests simultaneous clamp actuation and sheet insertion, not granular separation or agitation.

comparisons.objective: Load four square blanks into a close-clearance gravity magazine.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated grasping, planar squaring, close-clearance insertion, and stacking.
comparisons.success_condition: Each blank wholly inside, flat, supported, centered, and at rest; score is loaded count over four.
comparisons.reason: Although gravity and openings are involved, it tests individual precision insertion into one channel, not separating a mixture by inducing selective passage.

comparisons.objective: Fit a funnel to a bottle and pour beads through it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Funnel placement, jug grasping, controlled pouring, and narrow-mouth granular transfer.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 22 of 24 beads settled inside the bottle for 1 second for full credit; no retention class or spill penalty is specified.
comparisons.reason: Shares bulk pouring of free rigid particles, but its tested ability is guided one-destination transfer. The candidate additionally requires aperture-selective passage, transverse bridging and bridge release, washer retention, bimanual screen control, reseating, and immutable spill/contamination constraints.

comparisons.objective: Saw a true mitre while holding moulding against a mitre-box fence, then clear the work.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual workpiece restraint, guided reciprocating tool motion, and tool/workpiece handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Specified kerf depth or cut-through at the mark and angle, followed by saw return, workpiece removal, and arm clearance; simulation approximates cutting by stroke rules.
comparisons.reason: Guided cutting and workpiece restraint do not exercise granular flow, selective screening, or media recovery.

comparisons.objective: Classify machined blocks with a go/no-go gap gauge and sort them into trays.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated gauge alignment, test insertion, binary classification, and object placement.
comparisons.success_condition: All seven blocks in their correct trays for full credit, with penalties for false accepts/rejects; later versions also require evidence of gauge testing.
comparisons.reason: Both use size-related openings, but this task individually gauges and relocates discrete workpieces. The candidate physically separates a mixed bulk charge through a screen while retaining every larger part and managing bridges and spill.

comparisons.objective: Roll a wide cabinet shelf through a narrower face-frame opening and lower it onto four pins.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual reorientation of a large rigid body through constrained geometry and precise support placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Shelf level and seated on all four pins, cabinet undamaged, hands released, and stable.
comparisons.reason: Constrained large-body reorientation and placement are unrelated to selective granular passage through many apertures.

comparisons.objective: Place a carton on a shelf obstructed by a leaning glazed picture without damaging either.
comparisons.physical_skill: Obstacle-aware manipulation, stabilization or repositioning, and careful shelf placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Carton properly supported on the shelf, picture safe and stable, with damage/drop conditions enforced; versions refine clearance and release.
comparisons.reason: Tests fragile-obstacle handling and placement, not granular separation, agitation, or retention.

comparisons.objective: Measure a burger patty's center temperature through a side entry while stabilizing it with a turner.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization and controlled probe insertion with depth and angle control.
comparisons.success_condition: Probe tip reaches and remains near the center without breakout or excessive patty motion, followed by safe withdrawal and tool release.
comparisons.reason: Force-controlled probing of one workpiece does not overlap with screen manipulation and bulk particulate flow.

comparisons.objective: Load, uncap, re-cap, and cock a pen lancing device.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential snap removal, small-part insertion, twist-off fracture, snap refit, and sprung-slide actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Lancet seated, tab removed, cap fitted, device cocked and released; unsafe proximity to the exposed needle or dropping the device fails.
comparisons.reason: Multi-stage small-device assembly is materially different from size-selective granular separation.

comparisons.objective: Fit a sprung cage nut into a marked rack-rail hole.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hook one lip, compress the other with a screwdriver, rotate and seat a small sprung component bimanually.
comparisons.success_condition: Both lips sprung out around the marked hole, nut centered and flat, tools withdrawn, and state stable for 1 second; wrong-hole seating, dropping, or bending fails.
comparisons.reason: Tests spring-latch insertion with a hand tool, not particulate screening or granular-flow control.

comparisons.objective: Clear a towel from a rice-cooker steam vent and start the cooker.
comparisons.physical_skill: Remove an obstruction, place it safely, and actuate a sprung button.
comparisons.success_condition: Vent clear, COOK activated, towel supported, button released, and grippers withdrawn for 1 second; covering the vent while running permanently fails.
comparisons.reason: Obstruction removal and button actuation do not test separation of mixed rigid bodies through a screen.

comparisons.objective: Move an iron to the right end of a mat and leave it safely standing on its heel.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safe grasp, transport, reorientation, and stable placement of a weighted appliance.
comparisons.success_condition: Iron upright on its heel in the target region and stationary; dropping or leaving it face-down on the bare mat fails.
comparisons.reason: Single-object transport and stable orientation are unrelated to selective media recovery and bridge-clearing.

comparisons.objective: Insert a battery with correct polarity and screw a flashlight tail cap tight.
comparisons.physical_skill: Close-clearance cylindrical insertion, counterholding, thread engagement, and sustained rotation.
comparisons.success_condition: Battery correctly oriented and inserted, cap advanced by at least 300 degrees to within 1 mm of seated, all parts stable; reversal, dropping, or forced seating fails.
comparisons.reason: Tests keyed assembly and threaded closure, not bulk flow through apertures.

comparisons.objective: Reload a long-arm stapler and staple two sheets together.
comparisons.physical_skill: Open and hold a sprung magazine, align a staple strip, close it, position sheets, and actuate the stapler.
comparisons.success_condition: Stapler loaded and both sheets joined by a driven staple, with arms clear and mechanisms stable for full credit.
comparisons.reason: Sequential tool loading and fastening do not exercise granular screening or selective retention.

comparisons.objective: Safely remove a low toast slice using wooden tongs after unplugging the toaster.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safety-state change, lever holding, tong manipulation, extraction, and placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Toast on the plate, toaster unplugged, prohibited fork unused, lever and tongs returned, and arms clear; versions vary whether electrical state affects scoring.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual extraction with a grasping tool is different from bulk particulate separation and agitation.

comparisons.objective: Pour mixed coins from a jar and sort pennies and quarters into separate frames.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled bulk pouring followed by visual denomination classification and individual nonprehensile pushing of thin objects.
comparisons.success_condition: Per-coin final-state credit for each penny or quarter wholly inside its designated frame; no spill, damage, release, or dwell requirement is specified.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest generic sequence because both start by pouring a mixture and end with separated classes. Its tested separator is visual identity plus individual pushing, whereas the candidate tests physical aperture selection, orientation-dependent passage, bridge clearing, bimanual screen control, complete washer retention, and loss-sensitive recovery.

comparisons.objective: Wring a strep-test swab against its tube while rotating it, then withdraw it under squeeze.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual compliant-container squeezing, repeated swab rotation, and coordinated withdrawal.
comparisons.success_condition: Required squeeze/contact and extraction state with liquid preservation; versions specify rotation and release measurements.
comparisons.reason: Liquid-sample extraction from a swab does not test dry particulate screening or tool-induced granular flow.

comparisons.objective: Rack fifteen pool balls tightly on the foot spot and remove the triangle without disturbing them.
comparisons.physical_skill: Collective rigid-body packing, bimanual rack manipulation, compression, and clearance-sensitive lift-off.
comparisons.success_condition: All 30 neighboring pairs within 0.5 mm, head ball within 5 mm of the spot, correct pack orientation, rack removed, balls still, and hands clear; disturbance during removal can latch failure.
comparisons.reason: It shares multi-object contact management and careful tool removal, but tests dense packing rather than selective aperture passage, bridge release, and recovery of one constituent while retaining another.

comparisons.objective: Join two boards evenly on three glued dowels.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual multi-pin alignment, even pressing, wedge avoidance, and released seating.
comparisons.success_condition: Both seam corners within 0.5 mm, edges flush within 1 mm, boards flat, and grippers released and still for full credit; earlier versions use square sockets and later versions round bores.
comparisons.reason: Multi-feature insertion and seating of rigid assemblies do not overlap with bulk granular separation.

comparisons.objective: Rotate and stop a suspended humanoid torso at a target heading.
comparisons.physical_skill: Momentum-aware pushing/catching of one freely swiveling heavy load.
comparisons.success_condition: Torso stopped near 180° without collision, blow, or residual spin; 1 s dwell.
comparisons.reason: No pouring, aperture-based separation, granular bridge clearing, or retained workpieces.

comparisons.objective: Place caplets into selected organizer compartments and snap all lids shut.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-object placement plus bracing and operating snap lids.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct caplets in Monday/Thursday, other compartments empty, lids snapped, organizer stable and released.
comparisons.reason: Tests discrete compartment loading and latching, not size/orientation-dependent bulk separation through a screen.

comparisons.objective: Start a loose nail at a mark and hammer it flush.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual nail stabilization, impact control, hand withdrawal, and repeated hammering.
comparisons.success_condition: Nail flush, upright and on-mark; no bent nail or struck gripper; hammer released and 1 s stillness.
comparisons.reason: Impact-driven fastening is meaningfully different from controlled granular flow and selective retention.

comparisons.objective: Break a swab at its breakpoint while retaining its tip in a tube and binning the handle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Brace a light tube while applying controlled bending fracture to a slender shaft.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct break location, tip retained, handle binned, tube upright, objects released.
comparisons.reason: Controlled fracture and container bracing do not test screening, bridge release, or recovery yield.

comparisons.objective: Use a tweezer puller to remove a selected blade fuse and place it in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool pickup, narrow-access gripping, extraction against clips, and precise release.
comparisons.success_condition: Middle fuse extracted by the puller and released in tray; neighboring fuses undisturbed; tool set down and stable.
comparisons.reason: Selective tool-mediated extraction of one retained component differs from bulk media passage through apertures.

comparisons.objective: Remove a selected midget fuse from spring clips with a tong puller and tray it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Confined-access tool alignment, opposed-jaw grasping, and clip extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: F2 fully removed with the puller, released still in tray, puller put down; F1/F3 remain seated.
comparisons.reason: Tests constrained extraction rather than orientation-dependent granular separation.

comparisons.objective: Scan four groceries exactly once and transfer them to a bagging shelf.
comparisons.physical_skill: Reorient varied objects for barcode visibility, hand off between arms, and place safely.
comparisons.success_condition: Each item read once and released still on shelf; no unpaid transfer, duplicate read, drop, or loss.
comparisons.reason: Although it handles multiple loose objects bimanually, it lacks screening, aperture passage, bridging, and retained-versus-passed material behavior.

comparisons.objective: Seat a flexspline in a robot-joint housing with its teeth meshed.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine coaxial alignment, phase rotation, insertion, and cocking avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Teeth aligned and meshed, collar seated within tight pose tolerances, released and still for 1 s.
comparisons.reason: Precision keyed insertion tests mating geometry, not granular-flow control or mass recovery.

comparisons.objective: Hang two plates on separate moving conveyor hooks before a deadline.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed interception, hole-on-hook insertion, release, and settling on moving targets.
comparisons.success_condition: Each plate hangs freely, plumb and settled on its own hook for the final 1 s before the mark.
comparisons.reason: Dynamic hole engagement on moving hooks is different from passing many particles through a stationary screen while retaining parts.

comparisons.objective: Attach a grease coupler, pump grease without leakage, and return the coupler.
comparisons.physical_skill: Seal alignment, coupler operation, repeated pump strokes, and hose/tool management.
comparisons.success_condition: Required grease shots delivered while sealed, no leak, coupler returned to holder, arms withdrawn and final stillness.
comparisons.reason: Fluid servicing and sealed coupling do not exercise dry particulate screening or bridge clearing.

comparisons.objective: Cut a carton's taped seam without damaging the product and retract the blade.
comparisons.physical_skill: Knife actuation and long constrained-depth cutting with angle control.
comparisons.success_condition: Entire seam cut, product and cardboard outside tape unmarked, blade retracted; 3 s hold.
comparisons.reason: Continuous cutting and depth control are unrelated to granular separation and recovery.

comparisons.objective: Measure tire pressure with a pencil gauge and return the gauge to its holder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tight axial valve sealing, core depression, reading generation, and tool replacement.
comparisons.success_condition: Sealed 1.5 s press, 33–37 psi indication, gauge upright in holder, released and still.
comparisons.reason: Tests sealing and measurement, not manipulation of a screen or particulate mixture.

comparisons.objective: Couple a scaffold transom to a ledger at a marked position.
comparisons.physical_skill: Support and align a long member, close a hinged cap, engage a bolt, and tighten a nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Transom square and on-mark, cap shut, bolt slotted, coupler gripping, hands clear for 1 s.
comparisons.reason: Structural alignment and fastening are materially different from size-selective sifting.

comparisons.objective: Keep an automated loader's nest supplied one blank at a time.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated timed pick-and-place into a constrained nest while avoiding another moving arm.
comparisons.success_condition: Five blanks correctly presented and carried to the chute; no arm collision or double loading; 1 s success hold.
comparisons.reason: Both involve multiple workpieces, but this tests synchronized replenishment, not physical separation by aperture and granular agitation.

comparisons.objective: Store glasses in a sliding-lid box, put keys in a dish, and close the box.
comparisons.physical_skill: Careful object placement, clutter avoidance, and guided lid sliding.
comparisons.success_condition: Glasses upright in box, keys in dish, lid shut; no tipping, guide loss, contamination, or disturbance; 1 s hold.
comparisons.reason: Discrete storage and lid manipulation do not test granular-flow recovery or screen-based retention.

comparisons.objective: Break a suction stopper's seal and place it in a soap dish.
comparisons.physical_skill: Confined grasping under a faucet, peel/lift against suction, and transfer.
comparisons.success_condition: Seal broken, stopper released still in dish, hands clear for 2 s.
comparisons.reason: Single-object suction release and transfer are unrelated to mixture screening.

comparisons.objective: Load an anesthetic cartridge into a dental syringe and set its harpoon.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orientation-sensitive insertion, piston/harpoon engagement, force limitation, and precise rest placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Cartridge correctly oriented and seated, harpoon passes aspiration test, syringe on rest, hands clear; stopper not overdriven.
comparisons.reason: Tests delicate keyed loading and engagement rather than aperture-mediated material separation.

comparisons.objective: Measure a gauge block with a stand-mounted micrometer using its ratchet and lock.
